What if I told you Brooks Running started out making ballet slippers and bathing shoes? Founded in 1914, the Seattle-based company spent decades making just about everything except running shoes, moving from baseball cleats to roller skates, football cleats and children’s shoes, and softball cleats. It wasn’t until 1972 that Brooks made running its focus, and the company has been refining the category ever since.
Brooks introduced one of the industry’s earliest uses of EVA foam, developed the first running shoe with a breathable GORE-TEX upper, and introduced the Kinetic Wedge, which was an innovative design catered to women’s anatomy.
So, while Brooks may not be the trendiest brand, it has built a reputation for dependable support, comfort, and durability. Here at WIRED, Brooks has plenty of fans, especially for trail running and gravel running. The company also offers apparel we regularly recommend, including sports bras, outerwear, and running bottoms.
Brooks Running shoes are relatively reasonably priced for performance running footwear, with many models hovering around $150. If you’re in the market for a new pair, I’ve rounded up the best Brooks Running promo codes and Brooks Running coupons worth checking out.
Score 20% Off Your First Order With Brooks Promo Code
If you’ve never ordered anything off Brooks’ website before, new customers get 20% off their first order after subscribing to emails. You can apply the one-time Brooks coupon code for top-selling shoes, like the Caldera 7 and Adrenaline shoes, along with other gear and apparel. It’s an easy way to save on some of their top products to take your road and trail running game to the next level.
More Brooks Coupons and Offers
Are you already a member of Brooks Run Club? If you sign up, you get member perks, like early access to sales, standard free shipping with no order minimum, and free express shipping on orders from Brooks. Membership also includes more runner-specific perks, like a free birthday gift, an opportunity to earn prizes by syncing your fitness tracker and contributing research to the Brooks team. You can also win a chance to visit the Seattle flagship store and have your gait analyzed by Brooks’ team. To join, visit Brooks Run Club and register for the Brooks promo code.
If you shop and buy a complete outfit in one transaction from one of Brooks’ recommended buying guides—like Warm Weather Running Outfits or Fall Weather Running Outfits—you can get 15% off automatically applied during checkout. This is a fantastic deal if you only just realized in the past 10 days that you’ve been running in hail in your tiny shorts and cropped sports bra.
Save on Our Favorite Brooks Running Shoes
Brooks makes so many iconic running shoes that it’s hard to list them all. I’m currently running in the Brooks Glycerin Max, which is one of the cushiest shoes that I’ve ever tried. I don’t feel particularly stable on uneven terrain, but the padding is noticeably springy and cushy if you’ve been putting in some serious miles. WIRED director Michael Calore is a fan of the Brooks Ghost line, and if you’re planning on hitting the trails in the cold, wet Pacific Northwest, I would suggest the Brooks Cascadia Gore-Tex. The Adrenaline is the company’s most popular shoe.
Preorder Your Favorite Glycerin Now
One of the most anticipated Brooks drops is the Glycerin line. These shoes are made to be durable, while allowing freedom of movement and flexibility. The cushioned shoes are comfortable for running and movement on many types of terrain. Tons of shoes in the Glycerin line are available to preorder, including the Glycerin Flex, Glycerin 23, and Glycerin GTS 23. Be sure to check out the Glycerin line to see which is best for you.
The Cascadia Elite Available Now
Brooks is constantly dropping new shoe styles, ensuring there’s a type of shoe for every runner. The new Cascadia Elite Brooks Running shoe is unisex and great for trail running: with PEBA cushioning, a Vibram Megagrip Elite outsole, and a MATRYX engineered woven upper with Kevlar fibers to help secure your feet firmly, no matter what terrain you’re traversing. This shoe has a light, springy cushioning that helps to propel you forward, whether that be from competitive trail racing, to Sub-ultras to VKs to ultras.
Upcoming Brooks Sale Events to Watch Out For
Do you have a runner in your life? The odds are, they’re taking stock of their winter apparel and shoes and trying to decide if these leggings are going to make it through another winter season. The best time to save is during seasonal sales, with discounts on footwear and apparel, including discounts on popular items like the Ghost 16 running shoes.
Do you have running military, nurses, or first responders in your life? Brooks Running also offers 25% off Brooks promo code full-priced items for verified community heroes. Sign up here.
Brooks Discount: Shop Pre-Owned Shoes at Brooks
If you’re looking for a new pair of shoes, but don’t have the cash to invest in a brand new, high-end pair, look no further than Brook’s restart page, where gently-used Brooks shoes are on sale for deeply discounted prices. They have both men’s and women’s sections, recently added shoes, and a breakdown of bestselling styles, including the Adrenaline, Ghost, Glycerin, and Hyperion.
Brooks Coupon: 20% Off Join the Brooks Run Club
If you’re looking to shop at Brooks, it’s a great idea to join the Brooks Run Club for additional perks and discounts. Some of the best things Run Club offers are discounts of 20% off apparel when you join and an annual birthday gift. You’ll just need to log in or join the club for the discount code.
Brooks Sports Medicine Ambassador Program: 40% Off
If you’re a sports medicine professional, you can save big and get rewarded at Brooks Running. The Brooks Sports Medicine Ambassador Program is a free membership program for eligible sports medicine professionals as a way to say thank you for the care they put into runners and athletes. All you have to do is verify your status by signing in or creating an ID.me account to verify the applicant’s qualifications. Then, you’ll get a steep 40% Brooks discount on the first $1,000 spent on eligible items on Brooks Running online orders (it resets every January 1).
Brooks Return Policy and 90 Day Wear Test
Brooks knows how important gear is for the athlete. So, you can take your Brooks gear for a 90-day trial run, and if you aren't satisfied, return them for free. If you’re at all unsatisfied with your Brooks purchase, you can return it for free, with no shipping or re‐stocking fees.

North Korea and Russia open first road bridge linking both countries
- Published
The first road bridge linking Russia and North Korea has opened, allowing the two countries to more easily move cargo and passengers between their border across the Tumen river.
Pyongyang state media said the bridge will be used for "personnel exchanges, tourism and trade".
But Ukrainian OSINT group Truth Hounds said the bridge is intended "primarily to establish a covert military logistics corridor" to support Russia in the Ukraine war.
It comes as relations between both countries have grown since the start of the Ukraine war, with Russia's Putin and North Korea's Kim Jong Un previously pledging that both countries would help each other in the event of "aggression" against either country.
Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin described the bridge as a "new symbol of friendship", while North Korea's Prime Minister Pak Thae Song said it was a "historical event".
Up to 300 vehicles and 2,323 people can cross the bridge daily, Russian state news TASS reports.
Satellite imagery reported by the BBC in May this year showed the kilometre-long bridge alongside several new access roads, a border checkpoint, support infrastructure and parking facilities.
There are existing air links, as well as the rail link between the two countries, but until now the only road link was a makeshift solution where, by special arrangement, wooden planks were placed on the rail bridge to allow cars to travel over it, according to Reuters.
The Russian government said the bridge will initially be used to transport cargo, Reuters reported, before opening to passenger traffic later this year.
The bridge would provide, a "powerful impetus for the further development of trade, economic, scientific, technological and cultural cooperation," said Mishustin.
Appearing at the opening ceremony via video link, he described ties between Moscow and Pyongyang as being "at an unprecedented high level."
The most immediate impact may be increased export of weapons to Russia.
Researchers at South Korea's spy agency estimates that North Korea has already transferred $7 to 14 billion dollars' worth of rockets, missiles, artillery shells using ships. An estimated 11,000 North Korean troops are actively fighting Ukrainians in Russia.
Truth Hounds said in a recent statement that given the strategic partnership treaty between the two countries in 2024 - the bridge could be used to transport North Korean military personnel, construction workers and senior military officials directly to Russia.
It would also enable the flow of Russian technology and resources in the opposite direction".
Construction started in 2025, after the agreement to build the bridge was made during Putin's 2024 visit to North Korea, his first trip to the state in 24 years, which resulted in the partnership treaty. The bridge took 495 days to complete, after delays.
Russian tourists have trickled into North Korea since they were allowed in in 2024. North Korea has been hosting them in capital Pyongyang and the beach resorts of Wonsan-Kalma, while continuing to block those from other countries.
The road is also expected to transport North Korean labourers to Russia.
Around 10,000 North Koreans are working in Russia's construction sites and logging camps, according to a South Korean estimate. Although the UN bans countries from using North Korean labour, many enter Russia under the guise of student visas.
"The speed of construction is a reflection of the volume of trade activity between the two sides," Victor Cha from the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) think tank, told BBC Verify in May this year.
"This is spurred largely by North Korea's provision of troops, weapons, munitions, and labourers for Putin's war in Ukraine," he said.
"It is fair to say that this connection, prior to the war in Ukraine, was one of the sleepiest links between North Korea and its two neighbours."

Going into the summer transfer window as Premier League champions, hope sprang eternal for Arsenal.
An opportunity to capitalise, encouraged by a sense at Emirates Stadium that their competitors were in transition because of managerial instability.
If ever there was a moment to strike in recruitment, this was it.
The plans were ambitious: a shortlist with more than 20 players on it. They were targets at Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid, even at Chelsea and Tottenham.
But as the window shut on Tuesday night, you could not escape the sense of unfulfillment - certainly from a section of supporters.
Arsenal's close season was one characterised by some unquestionable successes, but also riddled by difficulties and frustration.
Ahead of their home match against Chelsea on Sunday, BBC Sport details Arsenal's transfer window and whether manager Mikel Arteta, sporting director Andrea Berta and, perhaps most pertinently, owners Kroenke Sports Entertainment can deem their summer operation a success.
Why it became Guimaraes and not Anderson, Tonali or Scott
Bruno Guimaraes's £75m capture from Newcastle United was Arsenal's most eye-catching signing.
Heading into the summer, Arsenal were keeping abreast of Guimaraes' situation at Newcastle, although others were considered a higher priority.
For instance, their interest in Elliot Anderson was widely reported, but it was clear the England international was joining Manchester City.
Guimaraes' former Newcastle team-mate Sandro Tonali and Bournemouth's Alex Scott were also among the midfielders explored before a move for the South American accelerated.
At the ages of 26 and 23 respectively, Tonali and Scott are younger than Guimaraes, who turns 29 in November.
But numerous factors, including availability and price - Tonali joined Spurs for a minimum £92m - made their signings difficult.
Aston Villa's Amadou Onana was also among the options considered, but the Belgium international suffered a serious knee injury at the World Cup.
By mid-June Guimaraes, who had universal backing inside the Emirates, emerged as the club's primary focus.
Berta knew the player's camp well and Guimaraes was admired by Arteta, who had made it clear he wanted proven talent to take his starting XI - rather than the wider squad - to greater heights.
Berta used his strong relationship with Guimaraes' representatives to facilitate Arsenal's move, hence why Newcastle maintained they had had no direct contact from the London club until days before his move was completed.
It is not uncommon for Berta to lean on intermediaries to conduct negotiations, although the approach has had varying degrees of success.
For instance, Arsenal actively sought moves for Leicester City teenagers Jeremy Monga and Louis Page over the summer.
But sources insist that the lack of club-to-club discussions meant both players ultimately did not join Arsenal, with Monga eventually signing for Manchester City when he appeared to be on the verge of moving to the Emirates.
That said, Berta's success in pivoting the club towards a deal for Guimaraes when it became clear other targets were not viable was well received behind the scenes at Arsenal.
Konsa was first-choice defensive option
The signing of Ezri Konsa was equally complex. Konsa was viewed internally as Arteta's first-choice defensive option.
Arteta wanted players used to the rigours of Premier League football - hence the moves for Guimaraes, Konsa and the failed efforts to land Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.
Konsa's ability to play at right-back was also viewed as a major benefit. Arsenal considered signing an orthodox right-back, with Ivan Fresneda among the options, but Konsa's versatility was a key factor.
But Berta appeared reluctant to meet Villa's valuation. A week before the Konsa deal was confirmed, Arsenal made a £40m offer, which was duly rejected.
Sources claim the deal was eventually sealed by the ownership at both clubs, and the transfer was agreed at £51m, with £4m in add-ons.
In the event of not reaching an agreement for Konsa, it is understood Tottenham duo Cristian Romero and Micky van der Ven were identified as targets – but Arsenal's north London rivals would not consider selling to them.
Como centre-back Jacobo Ramon is a player the club will continue to monitor, but clauses attached to his current contract make the deal difficult.
Tarik Muharemovic, who joined Leeds United, was another considered.
In attack, Christos Tzolis' impact since arriving from Club Brugge in a deal worth about £35m means the Greece international has been heralded as one of the discoveries of the summer.
It is understood the potential deal for the former Norwich winger was initially raised by an intermediary close to a senior member of the coaching staff during the close season.
Berta's number two, Maurizio Micheli, watched Tzolis play for his country against Sweden in June and was suitably impressed.
So far, the 24-year-old looks a positive addition to Arteta's squad.
Arsenal, who also made Piero Hincapie's loan deal permanent and signed Illan Meslier on a free transfer, are happy with the signings they have made.
The captures of Guimaraes and Konsa, who will both be 30 by the end of next season, have raised eyebrows given the combined £126m fee, amid concerns over how the pair's longevity may impact the natural evolution of the squad.
Yet it is undeniable that Guimares and Konsa add elite quality and experience to Arsenal ranks, and ultimately the club feel they paid the going rate to get those deals over the line.
Arsenal miss out on marque attacker
While the club delivered proven talent for Arteta in defence and midfield, Berta's remit of adding an elite attacker ended in disappointment.
Rogers was the club's primary target heading into the window, and the early indications were positive amid a strongly held view internally that the forward wanted to join.
At the start of the summer, it was Arsenal's understanding that Villa valued Rogers at £100m. Arsenal valued Rogers at £80m.
Berta, however, was confident of negotiating the price down to a level he and the club believed could get the deal done.
In the meantime, however, Berta explored alternatives - Bradley Barcola, Kenan Yildiz, Yan Diomande and Nico Paz were admired.
Anthony Gordon was a long-term target, but he had agreed before the World Cup to join Barcelona.
Yildiz and Paz will continue to be realistic targets moving forward. Eli Junior Kroupi is another the club will watch once he returns from injury for Bournemouth.
Anderson's move from Forest to City for £116m, however, altered the complexion of Villa's outlook on Rogers' future.
Villa increased their valuation to £120m and ultimately Chelsea ended up signing the attacker for £117m.
Arsenal, it is understood, were given the opportunity to match Chelsea's offer but refused, believing their £80m valuation was fair - but it does beg the question of whether Rogers would be a Gunners player now if Berta had acted sooner.
Ultimately, the failure to land Rogers arrived as the first of a series of blows to Berta in his efforts to deliver a top-class left-sided attacker for the team.
Arsenal genuinely believed they had a realistic chance of signing Vinicius Jr before he decided to sign a new contract at Real Madrid.
Berta and Arteta were all in on the Brazil icon. The club were prepared finance the deal too.
While the transfer would likely have cost a British record fee and been one of the most lucrative remuneration packages in Premier League history, the benefit to Arteta's team and the Brazil superstar's commercial value meant Arsenal were absolutely prepared to complete the deal.
Yet well-placed sources expressed to BBC Sport over the summer that Vinicius did not want to leave Real, while others feared Arsenal were being used to strengthen the attacker's efforts to secure a more lucrative contract at the Bernabeu.
Those concerns came to fruition as Vinicius signed a new long-term contract in Spain in another Arsenal disappointment.
There were similar reservations about Arsenal's well-documented pursuit of Julian Alvarez.
The Atletico Madrid forward showed very little indication that he was willing to join Arsenal; his preference to join Barcelona was one of the worst-kept secrets of the window.
But Atletico's point-blank refusal to sell to Barcelona was deemed reason enough by Berta and Arteta to persist with their interest in the hope of Alvarez changing his mind until the closing days of the window.
Alvarez, however, preferred to stay at Atletico, even though his relationship with the club is at an all-time low.
Did Arsenal waste their time with Vinicius and Alvarez? The answer varies depending on who you speak to.
When it became clear Alvarez was unlikely, Berta explored his options.
Intriguingly, Arsenal have admired Chelsea striker Joao Pedro, who was deemed not for sale over the summer, although there were concerns over how he would fit into Arteta's system.
It is claimed Berta relies significantly on his vast network of agent connections rather than acting on the club's existing scouting information when analysing the market.
For example, last summer, when all the scouting information pointed towards a move for Benjamin Sesko, Berta's arrival meant the club pivoted to Viktor Gyokeres, who is currently second-choice striker.
This summer the club's late dalliance with Lyon winger Malick Fofana provided a further example of Berta leaning on his agency connections after management agency Roc Nation offered Arsenal an opportunity to sign the Belgium international.
Berta's relationship with Roc Nation was particularly prevalent this summer given Arsenal's pursuit of Vinicius and the sale of Gabriel Martinelli, who are both clients of the agency.
It remains to be seen how much of an impact Arsenal's failure to sign a recognised top-level attacker impacts their season, particularly in light of Martinelli and Leandro Trossard's departures.
Arsenal will move towards player trading model
Arsenal headed into the window with a clear remit of ensuring the club become more sustainable and adept at trading.
Part of that directive is to ensure the club remain compliant with domestic and European financial regulations.
Depending on who you talk to, the size of the potential deals for Vinicius or Alvarez would have raised doubts over Arsenal's ability to stay within the regulations.
Nevertheless, ensuring they maximised the benefits of player trading will become an increasing part of Arsenal's financial operation in the future.
There was already evidence of that through the sale of Martinelli, whose £60m exit to Al-Hilal was the club's record departure. Arsenal have also secured a sell-on clause in the deal.
The exits of Martinelli, Trossard, Gabriel Jesus, Christian Norgaard, Jakub Kiwior, Fabio Vieira and Karl Hein secured the club in the region of £114m.
Through intermediaries, a possible exit for Myles Lewis-Skelly was explored, with a fee of about £80m believed to have been mooted for the midfielder.
Manchester United, who were attracted to Lewis-Skelly's ability to play at left-back, were interested but ultimately deemed his valuation too high.
Of course, it is Berta's job to have a firm grasp on the level of interest in the club's players and their market value but, nevertheless, the thought of Lewis-Skelly's departure resulted in huge uproar from supporters.
As BBC Sport revealed last month, the Gunners resisted any temptation to sell Ethan Nwaneri on a permanent deal, the academy graduate landing a season-long loan deal to Borussia Dortmund that includes a January recall option if required.
The minimum £15m fee secured in Trossard's deal to Besiktas is also viewed as a good deal inside the Emirates given the Belgian turns 32 in December.
Having spent nearly £450m in 12 months, Berta's work in the market has helped the club deliver their first league title in 22 years.
Yet, despite the money splashed, there remain clear issues in the squad - certainly in attack.
The summer window has left many supporters feeling questioning Berta's body of work at Arsenal.
And with the average age of the squad increasing following the captures of Konsa and Guimaraes, can the current options build a dynasty of success before the club need to spend heavily again on regenerating the team?

Apple Event Live Blog: Here Comes the Folding iPhone
Get all the iPhone news as it happens. We’re reporting live from Apple Park, the company’s headquarters in Cupertino, California.
Good morning everyone! Welcome to our live coverage of today's Apple media showcase.
We will have two reporters on the scene at Apple Park in Cupertino, California, to bring you live coverage. You'll be hearing from Julian Chokkattu, Boutayna Chokrane, Lauren Goode, Reece Rogers, and Michael Calore throughout the event. We might have some special guests pop in as well. We’ll be posting frequent news updates here, with the highlights also going on our social platforms.
Apple's presentation begins at 10 am Pacific, 1 pm Eastern, and 6 pm in the UK. We have a complete rundown on how to watch the show and what to expect.
Come back approximately 30 minutes before the presentation starts—about 9:30 am in California—and you'll see the words on this page replaced by a feed of our live updates.
A Folding iPhone Today
The short version of what to expect: The folding variant of the iPhone should make its debut today. The word around Silicon Valley is that it’s expected to be named the iPhone Ultra and that it will likely cost more than $2,000.
We’ll probably also see a Pro version iPhone today, and we can expect the folding iPhone and the Pro models to go on sale later in September.
What about the base model iPhone 18? That might not arrive until early next year, though Apple might tease it today. The longer wait could be because of a number of factors, including rising manufacturing costs and the ongoing memory crisis affecting the whole PC industry. Also, delaying the next generation of cheaper iPhones—the 18, the 18e, and the Air—would give Apple an opportunity to promote its premium handsets more heavily.
It’s also likely we’ll see the newest Apple Watch and Watch Ultra models debut at today’s event.
Both the new iPhones and the new Apple Watches will be getting some additional capabilities enabled by Siri AI, the newest version of Apple’s artificially intelligent assistant. So, expect lots of talk about the beefed-up new chips in these devices as well as “on-device AI,” secure computing, and battery optimization. Siri AI is actually powerful and impressive in our testing of the beta version, but just like the various Siris that came before it, there are limits to how helpful it can really be in your day-to-day life.
Also notable is the list of things we’re not expecting: Apple’s various smart-home products that have been rumored to be close to release, including new HomePod speakers and a smart home device that’s used to interacting with Siri’s camera-based Visual Intelligence capabilities.
Along those lines are the rumored AirPods with tiny cameras in them that can be used, in conjunction with voice commands, to give Siri AI some additional context about what you’re looking at and inquiring about. Those earbuds might come today, but we could just as well see them at an additional event in late September or in October. (It’s likely the smart-home products will show up at the next event too.)
How to Watch
To watch the livestream, you can, of course, just hit Play on the video stream on this page. But it's better on the big screen.
You can watch it in your TV's YouTube app; just tune into Apple's YouTube channel. You can also watch it on Apple's own streaming app. If you have an Apple TV or any streaming box, just go into the Apple TV app. When you open the app, the livestream for the event should be displayed prominently right at the top. This works even if you don’t subscribe to Apple’s paid streaming service. Watching it on the television frees up your laptop screen so you can follow the live blog. Convenient!
We'll see you back here about half an hour before the event begins.

Mental health conditions that may develop following a traumatic incident could contribute to a higher risk of future cardiovascular issues such as non-fatal heart attack and stroke or a fatal cardiac event, according to new research.
"Traumatic events are common experiences and can include serious fires or explosions, physical assault, transportation accidents, the suicide or death of a loved one, and severe medical illnesses or injuries," lead author Jennifer A Sumner, an associate professor in the department of psychology at the University of California Los Angeles, said.
"Experiencing traumatic events can significantly affect mental health as well as cardiovascular health. Although most work to date has focused on PTSD and cardiovascular health, our research suggests that we should think about a wide range of mental health consequences when looking at cardiovascular disease risk after trauma," Sumner said.
The study, published in the Journal of the American Heart Association, examined national health registries in Denmark, looking at 2,19,866 adults who did and did not develop major heart or brain conditions following a traumatic event.
About 44,000 of the 2,19,866 participants experienced a non-fatal heart attack, non-fatal stroke, procedures to restore blood flow to the heart or cardiovascular death between 1995 and 2019.
Researchers compared 1,75,872 people who experienced a trauma but not a cardiovascular event to peers who experienced a heart attack, stroke, procedures to restore blood flow to the heart or cardiovascular death during the 24-year period.
A wide range of mental health conditions were considered as possible cardiovascular predictors, and machine learning was used to identify the 15 most important mental health disorder predictors of heart and brain outcomes.
Alcohol abuse was found to be the most important mental health risk linked to serious heart or brain conditions for men and women.
"For men and women, the most important psychiatric predictor of MACCE (major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events) was alcohol use disorders," the authors wrote.
"After a traumatic life experience, individuals may turn to alcohol to cope and help manage their emotions. Over time, this new behaviour might develop into alcohol abuse, thus increasing their risk of a serious heart or brain condition," Sumner said.
Mood disorders, including depression, were found to be strong indicators of post-traumatic psychiatric issues associated with cardiovascular outcomes for both men and women. However, mood disorders were a more prominent predictor for women, compared to men.
Psychological conditions that can arise after a traumatic event connected to a higher risk of heart and brain conditions in the future included PTSD, mental disorders caused by brain or physical issues, non-substance-induced confusion, different substance use disorders, personality disorders, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and anxiety disorders.

Australian social media users to be offered choice to opt out of algorithms
CANBERRA, Australia — Australian social media users would be given a choice to opt out of algorithms under proposed laws announced by the government Tuesday that would let users have more control over what they see on their social media feeds.
"We'll require social media platforms to provide user empowerment tools that give people over the age of 16 genuine and enduring choice about what they see in their feeds," Prime Minister Anthony Albanese told reporters in Canberra.
The proposed legislation would also protect children from content that promotes eating disorders, hostile ideas about women, pornography, crime, dangerous stunts and that causes serious mental health distress.
The move for more user control and to keep children safer online follows Australia introducing world-first laws in December last year that ban children younger than 16 from holding accounts on the world's largest social media platforms including Instagram, Facebook and TikTok.
"It gives users choice and it will hold the big tech companies responsible for inaction. If they don't follow our laws, they will face significant penalties," Albanese added. Penalties under the proposed Digital Duty of Care legislation could be as high as 109.2 million Australian dollars ($78.6 million).
Social media platforms would be required to send a notification to new and existing users offering them a choice over their default feed, a government statement said.
Users would be able to opt in to having their default feed include personalized content recommended by an algorithm. Alternatively, users could see the content of friends and creators they choose to follow.
Digital services including online games, apps and artificial intelligence chatbots would also be required to protect children from design features that have negative behavioral impacts such as addictive features and those that have an effect on self-esteem, the statement said.
In April, Australia's online safety watchdog said it was considering court action against Facebook, Instagram, Snapchat, TikTok and YouTube, alleging they are not doing enough to keep Australian children younger than 16 off their platforms.

Inside the White House on 9/11
John McConnell on his memories of working in the White House on September 11, 2001. Plus: American Pastoral by Philip Roth.
Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube
In this episode of The David Frum Show, The Atlantic’s David Frum is joined by John McConnell, the longtime senior speechwriter for President George W. Bush and Vice President Dick Cheney, to discuss their memories of September 11, 2001—25 years later.
Then, David ends with a discussion of American Pastoral, a novel by Philip Roth, and what we can learn about domestic terrorism from the book.

Frum: Thanks so much to my friend John McConnell for joining me today on The David Frum Show. This week’s book is also a contemplation of terrorism, but in this case, a contemplation of homegrown, domestic American terrorism. The book is American Pastoral by Philip Roth, published in 1997. In my opinion, probably his greatest novel.
American Pastoral tells a story of an American Jew whose daughter gets mixed up in extremist activity. The novel is narrated by a man named Nathan Zuckerman, who’s Roth’s recurring literary alter ego. And Nathan Zuckerman tells a story of his childhood friend, Seymour “The Swede” Levov, a golden-boy athlete from Zuckerman and Roth’s hometown of Newark, New Jersey. The Swede seems to have it all. He’s a former high-school sports star. He marries a Miss New Jersey. He takes over his father’s successful glove-manufacturing business, and he settles into an idyllic life in rural Old Rimrock, New Jersey. He has one child, an adored daughter named Merry, M-E-R-R-Y.
Merry becomes increasingly politically outspoken in the course of the 1960s, when the novel is set. She gets involved in radical causes. She becomes increasingly dogmatic. Merry has a speech impediment, and somehow that concentrates her rage into forms of action that are beyond speech. And ultimately, that expressed itself when, in order to oppose the Vietnam War, Merry plants a bomb in the local post office that kills a local doctor. Merry then disappears, goes underground, and The Swede spends years looking for her.
When he finally tracks her down, she’s back in Newark, New Jersey, living in terrible filth and squalor, and she has converted to a form of ultra-pacifism. She becomes a Jain, J-A-I-N, a religion from India that is so opposed to violence that it refuses to kill even an insect. And The Swede has to contemplate how his beloved daughter could swing from one extreme of murder to this other extreme of pacifism almost beyond reason.
The Swede, who’s had this perfect life—sheltered from everything, coasting on inherited prosperity and success on an American dream in a country that has been a golden land for Jews like himself—he has to confront this eruption of what Roth calls “the American berserk,” the country’s capacity to burst out from anybody’s planned order into these forms of strange, bizarre personal violence.
Roth is here describing something very real. I mean, I went through, did a quick scroll through incidents that reminded me of the story of Merry Levov—of privileged people, people at every American advantage who lash out, who would adopt some scheme of or some personal ideology of extremist hate, and then lash out in violence against others. There’s so many examples of this. Let me just mention a few that just come to mind in the course of an ordinary search.
Remember Elliot Rodger? Elliot Rodger was the son of a Hollywood director. He grew up in very comfortable circumstances. He developed this ideology of misogyny; incel, I think, is the term. Misogyny, violent hatred to women. He killed six people and wounded 14 in a rampage, leaving behind a manifesto justifying what he did.
Or Patrick Crusius. He was the man who turned a weapon on a parking lot in El Paso to kill 23 people, motivated by his “Great Replacement,” anti-immigrant ideology. He also acted alone, and he also had a comfortable middle-class upbringing in Dallas, Texas.
Or Luigi Mangione—this is a perfect example of this—who comes from a prominent family in Maryland, and he gunned down an insurance executive in New York City. Again, for some crazy, bizarre ideological reason all his own, that unfortunately has found resonance in some of the more malicious corners of online life.
Or Ayman Mohamed Ghazali; I’ve talked about him before. He’s the Lebanese immigrant who settled in Michigan, was given the opportunity to make a life for himself in America, given the amazing gift of American citizenship, and instead took guns to Temple Israel in West Bloomfield.
You know, these people all have motives. They may be diagnosable as having some kind of mental illness, but they’re not so delusional as not to understand what they’re doing. But they’re acting on some script, some sense of grievance—the American berserk that Roth talks about—that pushes them in these directions.
And notice something else. They all have these remarkable resources and freedom. They have the resources to acquire weapons, and they have the freedom to conduct their work without surveillance. There are many societies in which people like this would be caught early because they lived in more of a surveillance state. Americans have freedom, resources. They have the ability to become whoever they are. And for most of us, the ability to become whoever we are is a great gift. It allows us to realize ourselves in all kinds of ways, in ways that people could not realize themselves even in countries that are comparably free but are not as supremely abundant and affluent as the United States.
But when you’re given the right to be who you are, that reveals something in some people that is berserk, that is bad. It allows, it gives you more scope to be indulged in wickedness and cruelty and hatefulness, to come up with some crazy set of ideas all your own, or that link in some other way. And to act out against your fellows in ways that bring hurt and harm and sorrow and suffering to the human species.
America gives all of us the means to be ourselves, and the question we all face is: Who will we be?
That’s it for this week’s episode of The David Frum Show. Thanks so much for watching. As ever, please, the best way to support the work of the show, if you can, is by subscribing to The Atlantic. Liverpool will reward Mac Allister if he lets his football do talking
- Published
The sheer ferocity of the strike to beat Jan Oblak was one thing, but the raw emotion shown by Alexis Mac Allister as he grabbed the Liverpool badge on his shirt and celebrated in front of the Kop told you all that you needed to know.
Just a day earlier, Mac Allister had spoken with a different kind of emotion inside the press room at Anfield as he expressed his sadness at Liverpool not offering him a new contract during the summer.
The Argentine, who is currently contracted until 2028, spoke passionately about his love for the club and the city and how he didn't feel like he had anything to prove - but there was an admittance that he needed to show the level he knew he could perform at.
Thankfully for Andoni Iraola and Liverpool, Mac Allister did just that by letting his football do the talking in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid.
From the outset against Diego Simeone's side, the midfielder seemed like a man on a mission. He blazed over early on from outside the box then picked up a booking just before the half-hour mark. Seeing Simeone wave an imaginary yellow card when he wanted a second booking for his compatriot just before half-time told a story in itself.
Simeone could only watch on when Mac Allister's left foot connected with the ball from outside the box and leave a diving Oblak with no chance - turning the game on its head after Marcos Llorente's opening goal and Dominik Szoboszlai's equaliser.
It wasn't quite like the strike that produced an actual seismic event - reaching a peak magnitude of 1.74 on the Richter scale - when Mac Allister found the top corner against Tottenham in 2025 on the day Liverpool won the Premier League, but it was more than good enough to beat one of the best goalkeepers in the world.
And it was certainly what Iraola and the Anfield hierarchy would have wanted to see after a below-par campaign from Mac Allister last season.
The understanding is that they were of the belief that Mac Allister's performances did not warrant the offer of fresh terms.
But if he can carry on like this, then it will be a question of when rather than if that offer is made for whoever replaces Richard Hughes - even if Mac Allister said he didn't know if his goal would boost his chances of a new contract.
"It was a lovely goal from Alexis and a lovely goal from Dominik Szoboszlai. It is good the midfielders can add goals," said Iraola, who smartly navigated a question about Mac Allister's future.
"We have midfielders that naturally they are going to arrive to the box - it is inside them and it is good we can also benefit offensively."
Former England goalkeeper Paul Robinson said on BBC Radio 5 Live it was "exactly what Mac Allister needed to do".
"If you don't get offered a new contract there's a reason, so what do you do? You go out and earn it," said Robinson.
"You work hard, you play to your level and he did that. He put himself about and popped up with a wonderful strike."
Five of Mac Allister's 20 goals for Liverpool in all competitions have now come from outside the penalty area.
Steven Gerrard knows more than most about playing in midfield and scoring from distance for Liverpool and he described Mac Allister's performance as "outstanding".
"Let your football do the talking," said Gerrard on TNT Sports. "Consistency, top performance, show your experience. Show you're a top international. This club will reward you."
Mac Allister himself said how it was a "positive step" for Liverpool as they won for the first time at Anfield this season on what was Iraola's debut as a manager in the Champions League.
"It was a good comeback," said Mac Allister on TNT Sports. "Overall, it was a good performance. Now we have to think about the next one.
"Before the game we spoke about the beginning of the first half and second half. I liked the mentality.
"I think we showed desire today. We got the fans behind us and that's really important when you play at Anfield. A positive step for us."
'We all know the qualities he's got'
Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock said Mac Allister just needed to be put into a system that suits him to get the best out of him.
"I don't think he has to show his importance to Liverpool, I think everyone knows the qualities he has got anyway," said Warnock, who was a pundit on Wednesday's Match of the Day.
"I think there will be a lot of talk about him because of what has gone on in the past few days, but I think Liverpool fans were already asking why hasn't he been offered a new contract when other players have.
"To come out and talk about a contract situation like he did, a couple of days before a game, and to be able to back it up the way he did with a good performance is important - but it is over the course of the season, where his performances are important because if he wants a contract and he thinks he deserves a contract then if his performances are good, he will get one.
"We all know the qualities that he has got - he is a World Cup winner, a Premier League winner, we know that he's a very good player, it is just he has got to be put into the right system to make it work.
"At the moment Liverpool's system is a little bit dysfunctional but it is starting to get better and he will get better because of that."

Uganda is withdrawing from the Duke of Sussex’s Invictus Games, the country’s military chief said, out of respect for King Charles amid division over the “Harry-Meghan nonsense”.
Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, son of the Ugandan president, made the surprise announcement in a post on X on Wednesday.
Kainerugaba wrote: “In order not to be construed as being opposed to His Majesty King Charles III of the United Kingdom, whom we deeply revere, Uganda hereby withdraws from the Invictus Games. We shall not participate in anything that does not have His Majesty’s approval.”
The timing of the post suggests it may be in response to an official letter to UK senior government and military officials on behalf of Charles which reiterated the Duke and Duchess of Sussex were not working royals and would not use their HRH styles.
When asked by the Times about what had motivated the move, Kainerugaba is reported to have said: “I have factions in the Ministry of Defence that support that Harry-Meghan nonsense. I had to quash it straight away. I support the monarch. Period.”
The news, first reported by Uganda Pulse news website, will undoubtedly be a blow to Harry, who two months ago stood alongside Uganda’s defence minister, Kiryowa Kiwanuka, at an Invictus Games event in London to announce that the East African nation would be the 26th country to enter the multi-sport event for wounded service personnel.
At the time, Kiwanuka credited President Museveni for his “visionary leadership” and Kainerugaba, a Sandhurst graduate, for “championing our teams entry” adding their support “marks a new chapter for our service men and women.”
The decision to withdraw may be an unintended consequence of the official letter, issued on Monday by head of the royal household , the lord chamberlain, Richard Benyon, at Charles’s behest, and clarifying the position of the Sussexes after their return to the UK two weeks ago.
The letter directed that the couple were “no longer working members of the royal family”, that their charitable work “is a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity,” and “their position is akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests.”
Kainerugaba was appointed army chief in 2024, and is widely seen as his 81-year-old father’s successor to the presidency. He has made several provocative posts on X, including threats to invade neighbouring Kenya, demands that Jay-Z hand over his wife Beyoncé so he could marry her, and threats against Bobi Wine, Museveni’s principal political rival.
The Invictus Games and representatives for the Duke of Sussex have been approached for comment.

Borthwick's holding pattern extended - with minimal confidence vote
- Published
"Horrendous" is not a word anyone wants to hear in their appraisal.
It was, however, the one chosen by Conor O'Shea, the man responsible for overseeing England's international success, to describe the men's team's 2026 Six Nations campaign.
And many fans will find it entirely apt.
England won only one match, their worst return since the tournament's expansion a quarter of a century ago. They lacked cohesion, discipline and tactical variety. It prompted profound, widespread questions about the future of head coach Steve Borthwick.
But, O'Shea revealed to Rugby Union Weekly, it has also preceded a contract extension for Borthwick.
Borthwick's terms now extend beyond the conclusion of the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia to the end of the Six Nations the following year.
The contrast of O'Shea damning England's performances in one breath, while committing more time and money to the man in charge of them will be curious to many.
But there is logic to it.
"You don't want the coaches looking for a job going into tournament," O'Shea explained.
"If they have no certainty, that is the worst case.
"So we'll give that certainty to the group, but then that will give us time to be able to look properly when it comes to the World Cup."
While New Zealand's swift renaissance under new coach Dave Rennie might give pause for thought, only the most disastrous dip in form would shake England determination to stick with Borthwick for that tournament in a year's time.
The extra six months added to Borthwick's deal beyond it is no fresh or significant vote of confidence though.
Nothing like the five-year extension that Ireland locked Andy Farrell into in June.
The RFU has instead just expanded a holding pattern.
It hopes to dampen the speculation that would surround Borthwick if the end of his contract was tied to that of England's World Cup campaign. It has also bought some time for a decision after the tournament.
It was a tactic that worked with the Red Roses.
As they closed in on their own World Cup title in 2025, the possibility that either a shock defeat or the satisfaction of lifting the trophy would prompt coach John Mitchell to walk away was tempered by the fact his contract had been similarly extended.
In the wake of victory, the RFU was able to take its time and tie him down to another four years.
On this point, O'Shea interestingly revisited another home World Cup.
In 2015, England were humiliatingly knocked out of the pool stages of their own tournament.
But, amid the hand-wringing and reviews, O'Shea believes the RFU was bounced too quickly into jettisoning a coaching group, which was led by Stuart Lancaster and also contained Farrell, Graham Rowntree and Mike Catt.
Their exit paved the way for Eddie Jones and Borthwick, fresh from shocking South Africa with Japan at the same World Cup, to come in.
"Nobody had the gumption to say they are the right people," O'Shea recalls of the Lancaster-led group.
He contrasted the RFU's decision at the time with New Zealand's faith in a coaching ticket that suffered a shock exit from the 2007 Rugby World Cup, but went on to lift the next two titles.
If England go out early in next year's Rugby World Cup, it will be difficult to find anyone advocating for a further contract extension for Borthwick, who was appointed in December 2022.
Having been handed a peach of a draw, England are unlikely to cross paths with South Africa, New Zealand or France until a potential final.
The semi-finals, at least, is par for England. Anything less and Borthwick is unlikely to make the cut.
A winning percentage short of 60% over nearly four years in charge and only fleeting success in implementing a more ambitious, expansive gameplan leaves little goodwill to fall back on.
Back in March, RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney explained that succession planning continued to identify the next England head coach, as it did for all senior roles at the organisation.
Sweeney knows the end of a Rugby World Cup cycle, when moves are made and the coaching carousel hits full speed, is when those plans are most often tested.
Despite Borthwick's public contract bump, they will be continuing at pace and in parallel behind the scenes.

At the Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026 in Mumbai, UPI operator NPCI announced a series of digital infrastructure initiatives to expand credit access across India. It also unveiled two AI initiatives aimed at streamlining enterprise fintech operations. Sanjay Lohiya, secretary of the Department of Financial Services (DFS), launched open-source android ATMs. These are designed to function as digital banking units (DBUs) in transit hubs and rural areas, as well as corporate parks and educational campuses, handling account openings, loan applications, and cheque deposits. They are also capable of instantly issuing RuPay cards and merchant UPI QR codes, reducing onboarding turnaround times from weeks to minutes. “The solution aims to expand the role of ATMs from just cash withdrawal and deposit machines to intelligent customer service and banking access points. Customers can receive their cards directly from the machine without waiting for courier delivery or making a branch visit, while merchants can obtain QR codes instantly for UPI-based payment collections,” the NPCI said in a statement. Nine major lenders, including State Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, and Slice Small Finance Bank, are trialling the ATMs alongside manufacturers Hitachi Payment Services, Perto India, and Vortex Engineering. NPCI’s AI Push The NPCI rolled out AiNxt, an open-source, enterprise-grade agentic AI platform designed to build, test, and deploy custom intelligent agents. The suite incorporates four core components: AiNxt OS, AiNxt Code (a plugin for integrated development environments or IDEs), AiNxt CLI, and AiNxt Enterprise. These will enable development teams to build, test, and deploy across IDEs and command-line environments. The platform can be used to build custom AI harnesses directly within existing development environments. Under a Bring Your Own Models (BYOM) framework, it enables AI agents to be deployed through low-code, no-code tools. Additionally, the NPCI also unveiled agentic orchestration & messaging (AtOM), an AI-driven agentic orchestration platform engineered to handle complex integration, change management, and partner onboarding across UPI. The platform produces digitally signed, machine-readable interactions to establish verifiable audit trails for compliance. Besides these, the NPCI is also expected to launch an ‘Unified Agent Protocol’ at the GFF. This would be a framework which would see AI agents execute small-ticket digital payments without requiring explicit user authorisation for every transaction. Finance Ministry Expands Scope Of Credit Line On UPI In addition to the above launches, the Ministry of Finance also expanded the ‘Credit Line on UPI’ facility to cover government-backed priority sector credit schemes, the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) and PM MUDRA Yojana (PMMY). The integration allows beneficiaries to link pre-sanctioned credit lines directly to UPI for digital merchant transactions. The overall credit base under these schemes spans over 7.7 Cr active KCC accounts with sanctioned limits exceeding ₹10 Lakh Cr and more than 57 Cr PMMY loans totaling over ₹40 Lakh Cr. Currently, ten banks have enabled Credit Line on UPI for KCC account holders, while eight banks have enabled it for PMMY beneficiaries, with more expected to join the ranks in coming months. The DFS also introduced the Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS) Three-Party Cash Deposit service, an interoperable assisted-banking service allowing depositors to deposit cash directly into third-party beneficiary accounts via local AePS Touchpoint Operators. The system relies on Aadhaar biometric eKYC authentication to verify the depositor and provides pre-transaction SMS name verification to prevent misdirected transfers. It aims to bring formal cash deposit facilities to rural, semi-urban and underserved customers. It also has added benefits like reducing travel time, validating the beneficiary and transaction, and assisting those who may not be digitally savvy. Fourteen institutions, including State Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, and YES Bank, have enabled the service.

Flash floods at the Nepal-Tibet border have killed at least 543 people and more than 1,500 are missing. Hundreds were foreigners in the area to work, take guided treks or make pilgrimages.
Thousands have been rescued, with some of the injured taken to hospitals in Nepal’s capital, Kathmandu. The number of missing may vary because of progress in the ongoing rescue efforts and differences in how data has been collected and verified among agencies.
Here is how different countries have been affected.
Nepal
Nepal’s disaster management authority said on Friday the death toll in that country had risen to 538, with 977 people missing. The authority said 3,253 people had been rescued by helicopter, and more than 150 of the injured were taken to hospitals in Kathmandu and the districts of Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading.
Local reports cited the National Emergency Operation Centre as saying on Thursday that the missing included 113 Nepali tourists, 85 personnel from the army and police, 161 residents from the Rasuwa district and one from the Nuwakot district.
China
State media reported on Friday that at least five people had died and 558 were missing in Gyirong County, Tibet. The state broadcaster CCTV reported that 260 of the 558 missing people were foreigners. In addition, nearly 100 Chinese citizens were missing on the Nepal side, China’s foreign ministry said.
India
India’s foreign ministry said 288 Indian nationals remained uncontactable, including 73 people who were working on a power project. Nepali officials said many Indian tourists were on pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a sacred site for Hindus.
US
The US state department said 90 of its citizens were unaccounted for in China and Nepal, but that it was not aware of any US deaths. Three Americans have been rescued.
Malaysia
Officials said 51 Malaysians were missing.
Ukraine
Ukraine’s foreign ministry said 55 Ukrainians were missing. The number includes two tourist groups, of 47 and seven people respectively, in addition to one Ukrainian woman travelling with a foreign tour group.
Australia
The Australian government said 39 Australians were missing.
Britain
Officials said 33 of the missing were from Britain.
Canada
The Nepal tourism board (NTB) said 25 of the missing were from Canada.
South Korea
South Korean government officials said nine citizens working on the construction of a hydropower plant in Nepal were missing.
Singapore
Eight Singaporeans were missing, according to the NTB.
Germany
The NTB said eight tourists from Germany were missing.
Russia
The Russian embassy in Nepal said eight of its citizens were missing.
South Africa
The NTB said six South Africans were missing.
Latvia
The NTB said six tourists from Latvia were missing.
Japan
Japanese media said five Japanese tourists were missing, made up of a couple and their children.
New Zealand
Five people from New Zealand were missing, the NTB said.
France
The NTB said four French citizens were missing.
Belgium
The NTB said three people from Belgium were missing.
Spain
The NTB said three visitors from Spain were missing.
Others
The NTB said two people each from Italy, Kazakhstan, Portugal, Ireland and the Netherlands were missing. It said 10 others – one each from Belarus, Finland, Hungary, Israel, Lithuania, the Philippines, Bulgaria, Switzerland, Serbia and Sweden – were also missing.

An Egyptian court sentenced a well-known television presenter and 11 others to death for manufacturing and trafficking narcotics in a sprawling drug case, official media reported on Saturday.
The presenter, Sarah Khalifa, 39, is best known for her programme Mission Impossible, which dealt with issues concerning security and crime.
The state-linked Al-Ahram newspaper said a Cairo court sentenced “Khalifa and 11 other defendants to death by hanging on charges of forming an organised criminal gang specialising in procuring materials used in manufacturing narcotics, with the intent to traffic them, and possessing and carrying unlicensed firearms and ammunition”.
The verdict came after the court consulted the Grand Mufti of Egypt for his religious opinion, a procedure required by Egyptian law in capital cases.
The verdict is subject to appeal.
Khalifa also owns a cosmetic surgery clinic and a production company that specialises in organising parties and events.
According to the state-run Akhbar el-Yom newspaper, the defendants were charged with “manufacturing synthetic drugs with the intent to traffic them, by importing the materials used in manufacturing from abroad”.
Al-Ahram reported that authorities seized more than 750kg of narcotics and raw materials, and found two apartments used as laboratories as well as unlicensed firearms and ammunition.
The court also sentenced Khalifa and others to five years in prison over a separate case involving the kidnapping and assault of a young man.
Egypt applies the death penalty for premeditated murder, terrorism, some rape offences and drug trafficking.
According to the Egyptian Commission for Rights and Freedoms, 541 death sentences were issued in Egypt in 2025.

The Bengaluru City Police have launched ‘Project Khushi’, a structured health and wellness programme aimed at supporting the long-term physical and mental well-being of police personnel, Home Minister Priyank Kharge said on Tuesday.
The programme will initially be implemented in the Electronics City police division, covering around 600 police personnel. Each batch will undergo a three-month programme comprising health check-ups, expert-led guidance sessions, and digital engagement activities.
The initiative will focus on preventive healthcare, nutrition, physical activity, quality sleep, and stress management, besides other lifestyle factors crucial for the long-term well-being of police personnel.
Pilot programme shows encouraging results
According to the Home Minister, an earlier pilot programme conducted as part of Project Khushi produced encouraging results. Around 61% of participants recorded a reduction in blood sugar levels, while 70% corrected Vitamin B12 deficiencies. In addition, 59% of participants reduced their body weight.
Mr. Kharge said that the results demonstrate that sustained and scientifically designed health interventions can have a positive impact on the well-being of police personnel.
Partnership with health and corporate organisations
“Our police personnel work every day in challenging and stressful conditions to ensure the safety of our communities. It is essential to pay continuous attention to their health. Healthy police personnel are the backbone of an effective and resilient policing system,” Mr Kharge said.
He added that equal importance must be given to mental well-being, a healthy lifestyle, and stress management, along with physical health.

Quick Answer
iOS 27 adds a native Custom EQ for compatible AirPods with an H2 chip or later. Go to AirPods settings > Audio and Routing > Equalizer > Custom, then adjust lows, mids, and highs to tune bass, vocals, and treble to your taste.
Apple has officially started rolling out iOS 27 for eligible devices, and it brings a lot of useful additions. If you are using any Apple audio product, iOS 27 gets a new native custom equalizer to fine-tune the music from your AirPods and other Apple audio products (requires Apple’s H2 chip; you can see full compatibility here).
In this guide, you will learn how to use the new custom EQ for your AirPods and other Apple devices.
Table of Contents
How to Use the New AirPods Custom EQ in iOS 27
The new native equalizer is only available in the latest iOS 27. If your iPhone is eligible for the latest iOS 27, you can go to General > Software Update and update to the latest iOS 27.
Custom EQ Supported Device List:
Custom EQ for Apple iOS 27 is only available for audio devices with an H2 chip or later. Here is the official compatibility list.
- AirPods Pro 2
- AirPods Pro 3
- AirPods 4
- AirPods Max 2
Now, if your device supports it, follow the steps below.
First, Update Your iPhone to the Latest iOS 27
Step 1: Open Settings on your iPhone.
Step 2: Scroll down.
Step 3: Tap on General.
Step 4: Tap on Software Update.
Step 5: Tap on Update Now (if the update is available).
Please ensure that your iPhone is on the iOS 27 eligible device list.
Next, Update Your AirPods Firmware
Step 1: Connect your AirPods to your iPhone.
Step 2: Open Settings on your iPhone.
Step 3: Tap on your AirPods (you will see this option if your AirPods are connected to your device) and next go to Step 5.
Step 4: If you don’t see it, open Bluetooth.
Tap on the “i” icon next to your AirPods.
Step 5: Now, scroll down and tap on AirPods Beta Updates.
Step 6: Enable the option that says AirPods Beta Updates.
Ensure your iPhone is connected to the internet and your AirPods are connected to your iPhone. Your AirPods will automatically update to the latest software.
How to Use the Custom Equalizer on iOS 27
Step 1: Open Settings on your iPhone.
Step 2: Scroll down and tap on your AirPods.
Or else, you can go to Bluetooth and tap on the “i” icon next to your AirPods.
Step 3: Scroll down and tap on Audio and Routing.
Step 4: From here, scroll down and tap on Equalizer.
Step 5: Select the Custom option.
Step 6: Now you can adjust lows, mids, and highs based on your preference. You can move the slider to the top and bottom. The line above refers to high, and the line below refers to low.
1. Lows: Increase or decrease bass.
2. Mids: Meant for vocals, where you can increase or decrease the vocal presence, especially if the music has singer vocals.
3. Highs: Treble, which AirPods are mainly known for. You can adjust treble sound using high settings.
Step 7: If you want to reset, tap on the Reset option.
Step 8: If you don’t want custom controls, you can tap on “Recommended,” and it will use Apple’s default recommended sound signature.
Currently, the iOS 27 custom equalizer is very basic. Even though Apple has the best ecosystem, Apple only decided to give you basic controls to customize the sound output from your audio devices.
I know most people are fine with the default settings on the AirPods, but sometimes even I prefer more control over the music.
Adding custom equalizer settings natively on your iPhone eliminates the need to download third-party apps, which sometimes have compatibility issues. However, Apple’s basic equalizer still leaves room for third-party options. Apple also offers you the option to reset the changes you have made.
This is a good start. Hopefully, in iOS 28, Apple will bring more features to this custom equalizer to fine-tune the sound signature of the AirPods. Using EQ does bring a noticeable sound difference. If you don’t see this option or are facing any issues, you can comment below, and I am happy to help you.
FAQs about iOS 27 AirPods Custom EQ
1. Does AirPods Custom EQ Work on iPad and Mac?
Yes, AirPods Custom EQ is also available on iPadOS 27 and macOS 27
2. Can You Save Multiple Custom EQ Presets for AirPods?
As I said before, current EQ settings are basic. As of now, you can only have one custom EQ profile
3. Does Custom EQ Work With Spatial Audio and Adaptive Audio?
Yes, it works with spatial audio and adaptive audio, but those settings are different from custom EQ. Currently, custom EQ only allows you to adjust lows, highs, and mids.
4. Does Custom EQ Affect Calls and Videos or Only Music?
Yes, AirPods Custom EQ applies to all media playing on your iPhone, including videos, music, TV shows, and much more.
5. Why Is the Custom EQ Option Missing on Supported AirPods?
If you don’t see the custom EQ option on your iPhone, make sure that you update to iOS 27. Custom EQ options are available for AirPods that have an H2 processor. At the time of writing this article, current supported models include AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods 4, and AirPods Max 2.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy visits Canada
Visit comes as Ukraine grapples with barrage of devastating air strikes
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is in Canada this week for his first visit to the country in nearly a year as his country copes with an onslaught of deadly airstrikes.
Zelenskyy will be in the country from Wednesday to Friday and attend events in Calgary, Toronto and North Bay alongside his wife, Olena Zelenska, says a statement from Prime Minister Mark Carney.
"The visit underscores Canada's continued leadership in supporting Ukraine and reflects our unwavering commitment to a just and lasting peace," Carney said in the statement.
The visit will focus on "shared priorities" between Canada and Ukraine, including deepening defence, economic and energy co-operation, Carney's statement said.
"It will also address the human cost of Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and build on the strong people-to-people ties that connect our countries."
The statement doesn't say when or where Zelenskyy is expected to arrive in Canada, but the prime minister's itinerary says he is meeting with Zelenskyy in Calgary on Thursday morning. The two leaders will participate in a signing ceremony and hold a news conference afterwards.
- Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expected to visit Canada next week: sources
- Carney prepared to tell Putin to 'get out of Ukraine' if Russia welcomed to G20 summit
The Ukrainian president announced that he was travelling to Canada in a social media post on Wednesday, but did not say what city he was flying into.
Zelenskyy's most recent visit to Canada was last December, where he met with Carney in Halifax before travelling to the U.S. for talks focused on ending the Russia-Ukraine war.
Carney visited Kyiv last August in his first official visit to the country, where he reiterated Canada's support for Ukraine and unveiled details of an additional $2 billion in military aid.
Flight delayed Tuesday due to drone activity
On Tuesday, a flight scheduled to carry Zelenskyy from Moldova to Norway was delayed when authorities closed Moldova's airspace because of a drone incursion, a government spokesperson said Wednesday.
Moldovan police said a Russian drone crashed on Tuesday in a sunflower field on the outskirts of a village in Riscani district, which caused four fires to break out but no injuries.
On Wednesday, government spokesperson Dumitru Ciorici said Moldova had closed its airspace on Tuesday afternoon to protect aircraft flying over the country at the time, delaying three departures, including Zelenskyy's.
Zelenskyy's visit comes as Kyiv copes with devastating airstrikes and as his government pleads for more air defence support. European leaders argue Russia has been widening its war.
Before travelling to Canada, Zelenskky chided the international community for not taking a tougher stance against Russia over its escalating bombardment of civilian areas of Ukraine.
"Unfortunately, there has been too little response from the international community to these strikes, which are taking people's lives practically every day," he said on social media.
"But a response is needed — Moscow must not go into the winter believing that it can get away with missile and drone terror without consequences."
Last week, Carney told reporters his message to Vladimir Putin will be straight forward if the Russian president attends this year's G20 summit in Miami.
"The message will be simple: 'Get out of Ukraine, give back all of Ukraine to Ukraine, end this war which is killing more than 30,000 of your people every single month,' and I'd leave it at that to be honest."
With files from The Canadian Press and The Associated Press

The prices of food items sold at multiplexes would continue to be set by traders with no scope for any governmental intervention in the price-fixing mechanism.
A Supreme Court order had termed cinema halls as private properties of its owners, who were entitled to “stipulate terms and conditions so long as they are not contrary to public interest, safety and welfare.” The court also noted that the owners were entitled to “determine the business model to be followed and to regulate the terms on which such sale should take place” in the K.C. Cinema vs State of Jammu and Kashmir case in 2023.
The issue of multiplexes charging “exorbitant prices” for snacks, including popcorn, had become a raging topic of discussion in Keralam with Thiruvananthapuram Mayor V. V. Rajesh flagging it. The officials of the Legal Metrology department in Keralam had held inspections in various movie halls and multiplexes across the State following the public resentment against the pricing.
Joint inspections by officials from the Legal Metrology, Civil Supplies and Food Safety departments were recently carried out in a few malls across the State on an instruction from Anoop Jacob, Minister for Food and Supplies, following the complaints.
At the multiplex in Kochi, a 90 g serving of regular salted popcorn costs ₹340, while the cheese and caramel variants are priced at ₹380 each. A 180 g serving of salted popcorn costs ₹420, and the cheese and caramel variants ₹460 each. A 240 g serving of salted popcorn is priced at ₹570.
A 90 g serving of nachos starts at ₹340, while a 170 g burger costs ₹260. A 540 ml bottle of cold beverage is priced at ₹290, and a vegetable sandwich costs ₹240.
“The MRP can be independently fixed by the manufacturers, and the law does not permit any governmental intervention in the process. We cannot insist on fixing the price of any products. All that the Legal Metrology Department (LMD) can do is to check whether the packaged products are sold at the MRP and the prescribed weight,” said Rajesh Sam, Controller, LMD.
The department can also insist that non-packaged products are sold at the price and weight as displayed in the menu cards, he said.
The Supreme Court, in a Bench comprising the then Chief Justice of India, Justice D.Y. Chandrachud, and Justice P.S. Narasimha, upheld the prohibition on carrying food and beverages from outside into the precincts of a movie hall, holding that it was not “contrary to public interest, safety or welfare.” The finding worked in favour of cinema hall owners, much to the chagrin of movie buffs.
The court observed that a movie hall also “doubles up as an eatery when food and beverages are sold within its premises.” “Patrons of a movie hall cannot demand to bring their own food to eat there when a condition to the contrary is enforced by the cinema hall owners. This would be akin to permitting a customer who visits a restaurant to carry their own food to that restaurant and eat it within the premises of that restaurant,” the court held.
The Bench also directed that hygienic drinking water be supplied free of cost within the precincts of the cinema hall. It further held that, in the case of an infant or young child, a reasonable quantity of food or beverages may be carried inside the hall.
