Volatile Trump may misinterpret BRICS Summit as anti-West, warns ex-diplomat Ajay Bisaria
Ajay Bisaria warned of a risk that the US could misinterpret the BRICS as anti-Western, while stressing that India will defend the grouping as a non-Western platform, instead of anti-Western.
As BRICS nations prepare to convene in New Delhi for the 18th Summit on Saturday, former diplomat Ajay Bisaria said there is a danger of the US interpreting the summit as anti-Western this time, while stressing that India remains firmly opposed to any attempt to turn it into an explicitly anti-Western platform.
Speaking at the India Today BRICS Roundtable, the former High Commissioner of India to Canada said New Delhi had worked to recast BRICS as a "non-Western" grouping rather than an "anti-Western" one.
When asked about US President Donald Trump's opposition to BRICS and his labelling of the grouping as anti-American, Bisaria said,"There is a small danger of the US misinterpreting it that way because of a very volatile White House and a very volatile Trump," and the engagement of China and Russia in the platform.
He added, "But I would say India, on this, is not going to be batting on the back foot. India is going to be on the front foot on strategic autonomy and defending the BRICS, uh, but there's always this small danger of it being misinterpreted." However, Bisaria noted that there is not a huge risk of a strong anti-Western message coming out of this BRICS summit.
Bisaria said there had been attempts in the past to push BRICS towards an anti-Western position, but that did not suit India."There were some instincts within BRICS in the past which tried to push it towards an anti-Western kind of positioning. That doesn't suit India, and India doesn't push it in that direction," he said.
He added that India had instead sought to change the "branding" of BRICS and present it as a grouping of non-Western countries focused on economic and developmental issues. "What India has been doing successfully is changing the branding to a non-Western grouping rather than an anti-Western grouping," he said.
Bisaria also said India's task at the summit would be more complicated than when it hosted the G20, given the presence of two active conflicts and the expanded membership of BRICS. Even so, he said he was optimistic that India would be able to secure consensus on a summit document, while cautioning that one contentious paragraph on Iran or Ukraine should not become the test of the entire meeting.
Geopolitical analyst Ashok Malik, who also joined the discussion with Bisaria at the India Today BRICS Roundtable, said the original BRICS had long carried a tension between two competing visions -- one that saw it mainly as an economic and developmental forum, and another that sought to give it a stronger geopolitical identity.
According to Malik, India has consistently backed the former approach, while Russia and China have at times sought to push BRICS in a more explicitly geopolitical direction.
"China and Russia have tried to nudge the group in the other direction, not very successfully. It's been a diplomatic tussle. I would argue that with an expanded BRICS, the idea of one common political position or geopolitical position, whether anti-West or pro-X or anti-Y, is that much more difficult because why just look at the West and the anti-West dynamic," Malik, partner of US strategic advisory forum The Asia Group, observed.
Malik said expansion would make a single geopolitical position even harder to achieve because the members themselves have sharply divergent interests. He said the inclusion of countries such as Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Iran made consensus on geopolitical questions particularly difficult.
The implication for India, he said, is that BRICS will have to focus on areas where members can find common ground, including economic cooperation, supply chains, development, climate change and resilience, rather than trying to establish a common position against the West.
The experts' remarks come amid growing US scrutiny of BRICS as the grouping expands beyond its original members and increasingly discusses issues such as de-dollarisation and reforms to the international financial system. India, however, has repeatedly maintained that BRICS is not an anti-Western alliance and that its participation is consistent with New Delhi's policy of strategic autonomy.
Last year, Trump criticised BRICS for pursuing what he described as "anti-American politics" and threatened to impose a 10 per cent tariff on countries that aligned with the grouping. However, he did not clarify or elaborate on what he meant by "anti-American policies" in his post.

SC directs reputation loss compensation for compulsorily retired bureaucrat
The Supreme Court set aside the Central Administrative Tribunal and Delhi high court orders and directed his farewell
The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed the government to pay ₹9 lakh in compensation for a bureaucrat’s loss of reputation after his compulsory retirement in 2018 on the grounds of questionable integrity, and to ensure a proper farewell at his office.
A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nadu directed that all emoluments, notional promotional benefits, and the ₹6 lakh that the former Indian Trade Service (ITS) officer SS Das incurred on the eight-year legal battle be paid to him.
The court ordered the Director General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) to call Das back to the office and give him the fitting farewell he deserved on his superannuation.
Das was issued a compulsory retirement order in May 2018 while he was the DGFT department joint secretary, five years before he was due to retire. The Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) and then the Delhi high court dismissed his challenge in January 2024, prompting him to move the Supreme Court.
The bench set aside the CAT and high court orders and directed his farewell with full honour and in the manner in which he would have received on the date of his superannuation. It said Das was entitled to all service benefits, including the notional promotion gained by any of his juniors during the period that he remained out of service.
The bench found that Das’s confidential service records marked him “outstanding” and “very good” throughout his career and the Union Public Service Commission recommended his promotion as joint secretary considering his excellent track record and uncompromising integrity.
The compulsory retirement order cited the action to be in “public interest” on account of the “questionable reputation and conduct”.
The bench found that the decision was based on an additional secretary’s note which the court dismissed as not being worth the paper it was written on. “The said note is not only bizarre, but sinister in its design. The immediate and inevitable question that arises on its perusal is, was the then additional secretary acting to protect the interest of the department or to espouse the cause of the representatives of the domestic industry,” the bench said.
The bench said such a note, bereft of any credibility, was made the foundation for showing the door to an excellent public servant who, by dint of his independence, integrity and courage, stood tall to ward off pressures from the domestic industry to protect the interest of the revenue.
“It does not require great intelligence to fathom the why and what of it, and as to who orchestrated the move for the marching orders to be given to such an officer,” said the bench, citing the service records. “We deem it fit to observe that this is a fit case, in which, the order smacks of arbitrariness, perversity and mala fides, warranting the case for judicial interference in full force.”
The order was passed under Fundamental Rule 56(j) even as the government argued that this provision grants discretion to the competent officer to act in public interest. The bench underlined that discretion is not a charter for arbitrariness. It added that reputation is earned by dedicating the best years of life to the service of the nation.
The bench said dismissing such a hard-earned reputation as “dead wood” smacks of a high degree of malice and a colourable exercise of power. It added that recourse to FR 56(j) should not be exercised lightly or casually. The bench added that it must be founded on credible, cogent material worthy of being acted upon and not on mere suspicion and conjecture.

CUPERTINO, Calif.—Apple’s new iPhone 18 Pro is an iterative update that—as usual—focuses heavily on both performance and new camera features. This time around, many of the new camera features are oriented around giving the user more direct control of the image, rather than depending entirely on Apple’s computational photography assumptions.
As usual, the new iPhone has a new chip. It’s called A20 Pro, and it’s the first 2 nm chip for the iPhone. It has a 6-core CPU, with two super-cores that are up to 20 percent faster, and four efficiency cores. A 7-core GPU offers up to 40 percent improved performance and increased bandwidth.
The A20 Pro also has a new Neural Engine—the machine-learning processor on the system-on-chip—which the company says is basically two Neural Engines on one chip.
Apple spent a significant chunk of the iPhone presentation talking up Apple Intelligence, arguing that the iPhone is a perfect place to establish and maintain the context for effective AI features—for example, with access to your calendar and daily habits—but of course tried to differentiate on the basis of privacy within that context. The company also discussed the previously announced new LLM-driven capabilities of Siri. Siri AI, as Apple calls it, will arrive in October.

Five dead and 86 missing as 'heartbreaking' fire breaks out on Philippines ferry
- Published
At least five people have died and 86 are missing after a fire broke out on a ferry in the Philippines, the country's coastguard said.
The MV June Aster, which set off from the capital Manila ferrying 117 passengers and 17 crew members, was nearing its destination at the tourist hotspot of Coron in the province of Palawan when it caught fire.
The blaze, which erupted at 18:00 local time (10:00 GMT) Wednesday, was still burning as of 11:00 on Thursday. The strong currents and poor weather were a challenge to those working to extinguish it, the coastguard said.
A first responder told the BBC they had never seen such a disaster in Coron, calling it "really heartbreaking".
"I was one of the people who carried and transported the casualties to the hospital last night," the first responder said, adding that the ferry was an hour away from its destination.
Video clips shared by the coastguard on Wednesday night showed the vessel engulfed in flames and people being pulled out of the water into rescue boats.
"Reports from our vessel indicate strong currents in the area," a spokesman from the coastguard tell the BBC, noting that the ferry had drifted from its initial distress location – four nautical miles off Barangay Turda – to a point 7.68 nautical miles away.
"It has been carried further out by the current. These are the challenges our personnel are facing in the search area."
The cause of the fire remains under investigation, the coastguard said, adding that it had not yet spoken to any of the 43 people who'd been rescued.
The survivors were taken to an evacuation centre in Barangay Turda, which sits just north of Marcilla. The state of their injuries is unclear.
Anelyn Magbanua is among those anxiously waiting for news of their loved ones.
Her husband Marlon had spent a few days in Manila visiting their two children, who were going to school in the capital city.
Magbanua last heard from him while the ferry was passing through a village about two hours from the port in Coron, she tells the BBC.
"I was expecting that the ferry will arrive at the pier at between 18:00 and 19:00 yesterday," she said, adding that she had gone to bed early but was awakened by a cousin who told her the ferry Marlon was on had caught fire.
"I couldn't describe what I am feeling right now. I have been crying and praying since last night," Magbanua says.
She'd travelled to a hospital in Coron, hoping to find Marlon among the survivors – but he remains unaccounted for.
"My two-year-old son and I are outside the hospital as we speak. We have nothing but ourselves," she says.
Rai Garcia has three family friends among those missing.
Mae Lorraine Galera-Navoa, who is the sister of Garcia's brother-in-law, had travelled to Luzon to attend her father's funeral, accompanied by her husband Elyzer Navoa and their three-year-old daughter Hiraya Joy.
They had been travelling home to El Nido in Palawan on board the vessel when it caught fire.
"We haven't received any news yet. That's why we had to comment on local news threads just to receive updates," Garcia says.
"We still hope and pray for their safety."
Garcia and his family made a poster to appeal for information of the family of three using a photo Mae had taken on the ferry and shared with immediate relatives.
Others have posted on the Philippine Coast Guard's Facebook page asking for information of their missing loved ones. "Please can you find my sibling," read one comment.
Maritime accidents are common in the Philippines, an archipelago of 7,100 islands.
Inter-island ferries are a cheap way to move people and cargo between islands, some of which are inaccessible by air.
But there is always the risk of severe weather, monsoon rains and typhoons which can cause turbulent conditions. The country is affected by an average of 20 typhoons every year.
Past accidents have also been blamed on poor maintenance and uneven enforcement of safety laws.
In 2023, 31 people died after a fire broke out at a passenger ferry in the country's south-western tip. The MV Lady Mary Joy 3 was on its way to Basilan island from Zamboanga city, a major port in the main southern island of Mindanao.
But with 86 still missing, this ferry disaster could prove to be among the worst to have happened in the Philippines in recent years.
Additional reporting by Joel Guinto

Laura Loomer warns JD Vance he’ll ‘regret’ it if he shakes Zohran Mamdani’s hand at 9/11 ceremony
‘It will be a photo you live to regret forever if you shake his hand at the 9/11 memorial,’ Laura Loomer, a right-wing provocateur, wrote on X
Right-wing provocateur Laura Loomer publicly urged Vice President JD Vance to refuse a handshake with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani at an upcoming 9/11 anniversary ceremony.
Loomer, an ally of President Donald Trump with a large social media following, made the plea Tuesday in a series of X posts laced with anti-Muslim rhetoric.
“I'm saying this from a place of concern: Mr. Vice President…Do not shake [Mamdani's] hand when you attend the 9/11 ceremony in New York,” she wrote. “It will be a photo you live to regret forever if you shake his hand at the 9/11 memorial.”
In a separate post, she wrote that the “most America First thing” Vance can do “on 9/11 is refuse to shake the dirty Muslim Mayor's hand.” She also baselessly characterized Mamdani as a “jihadist.”
“I'd rather chop my hand off than be caught in that photo,” Loomer added in a third post hours later. “I can't think of a worse photo opp.”
Vance is scheduled to travel to New York City Friday for a ceremony commemorating the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, which killed nearly 3,000 people. Like past mayors, Mamdani will be in attendance.
Mamdani, a democratic socialist and New York's first Muslim mayor, has faced calls from prominent Republicans to skip the anniversary event.
On Sunday, former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani, who was in office in 2001, told Newsmax that he opposes Mamdani attending the downtown event. “It offends me that he's coming,” Giuliani said before baselessly claiming that Mamdani supports a plot to “take us over” and compared him to al-Qaeda terrorists.
Earlier this month, former New York Governor George Pataki, who was in office during the attacks, told City & State that Mamdani should skip the event.
"With respect to the mayor, I think anyone who doesn't intentionally distance themselves from Hasan Piker, who has said that America deserved the attacks of September 11th, should not be there," Pataki told the outlet. Piker, a far-left streamer, is a vocal supporter of the mayor.
Conservative critics have also challenged Mamdani's appointment of Ramzi Kassem as the city's chief legal counsel, citing Kassem's past representation of a man whose brother-in-law was one of the 9/11 hijackers. The controversy intensified after The New York Post reported Saturday that, following the mayor's signing of an executive order designating September 11 as a "Day of Remembrance and Service," the ceremonial pen was handed to Kassem.
Mamdani, who has condemned the 2001 attacks as “horrific,” said he still plans to attend Friday's ceremony.
“I will proudly honor the families, the survivors, the first responders forever impacted by that horrific terror attack by standing alongside them at this year's 9/11 commemoration, reaffirming that we will never forget the solemn day felt by all of us who call this city home and, frankly, by all of us who call this country home,” he told City & State.
Also this week, he released over 170,000 pages of internal records that show officials misled people about the safety of the air around Ground Zero after the September 11 terror attacks.
“People got sick because the leaders they trusted lied and told them they were safe to breathe in toxic air,” Mamdani said during a news conference.
One prominent official who will not be in attendance on Friday is President Donald Trump.
According to The New York Times, the Republican president had initially planned to be there, but changed his mind after he was informed that no political speeches were allowed. After the story was published, Trump claimed that reporter Maggie Haberman had “made up the story.”
The president will instead commemorate 9/11 by attending a service at the Pentagon alongside first lady Melania Trump.

2 men jailed for up to 38 months over pro-independence group’s secession plot
Judge says pair, acting as advisers, devised ‘full plan’ to advance goals of Taiwan-based group calling for Hong Kong’s independence
Hong Kong’s District Court has sentenced two men with autism to up to three years and two months in prison for their involvement in a pro-independence group seeking to separate the city from Chinese sovereignty.
District Judge Ernest Lin Kam-hung on Thursday found that courier Chan Tai-sum, 27, and waiter Ng Chi-tung, 25, had been deeply involved in the Taiwan-based Hong Kong Democratic Independence Union between November 2024 and July 2025.
He said the pair had jointly devised a “full plan” to advance the group’s objectives, although it had not been carried out.
Founded by a fugitive, the union advocates Hong Kong’s “liberation” from mainland Chinese rule, seeks international recognition for a self-proclaimed “Hong Kong Parliament” and calls for the establishment of an army to “restore and defend” the city.
Both defendants had earlier pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit secession.
Judge Lin said the pair had served as advisers within the organisation. Chan was responsible for designing promotional materials, establishing ties with foreign organisations and compiling personal data on police officers and their families.

For the first time in 15 years, a new CEO took the stage at Apple's big fall event. Taking a page out of Steve Jobs' book, John Ternus announced "one more thing" — Apple's first foldable phone.
Ternus, a "product guy" who previously led Apple's hardware team, took over for Tim Cook at the start of the month. The annual product keynote marked an opportunity for the new CEO to introduce himself to the wider world of Apple fans — and pitch them on increasingly expensive gadget upgrades.
The foldable iPhone Duo, which is shaped like a passport, becomes an iPad-shaped device when it's open. It's Apple's biggest design change to the iPhone since Jobs first unveiled the phone in 2007.
Customers will have to pay big to own one of the devices, which opens for pre-orders on October 16 and launches on October 23. The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999.
Apple also announced it was raising the price of its high-end "Pro" iPhone lineup by $100, a few months after raising prices on MacBooks and iPads — the result, Apple says, of the bruising memory shortage. The new iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199 and the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299.
Apple also unveiled new Apple Watch models with new health-focused and AI features, the new AirPods 5, and detailed the many software features launching in iOS 27, which launches September 14.
Scroll on for a play-by-play of Apple's big keynote:
That's a wrap!
Apple wraps up its September hardware event after giving the final details for the foldable iPhone Duo, which CEO John Ternus introduced using Steve Jobs' famous "one more thing" line. Apple's stock is trading down 1% as the livestream concludes.
Thanks for joining us! See you at the next Apple event.
The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 and launches October 23

Local tribal groups from Gadchiroli have opposed the appointment of dreaded former Maoist leader Bhupati to Gondwana University as a coordinator. “Why are local tribals, who have worked for PESA, not being given the opportunity? An upper-caste man from outside Maharashtra who exploited tribals and led them to their deaths is being favoured for a job which involves empowerment of tribals. How can we trust him to spread awareness among tribals about PESA, and not anything else? We want the government to cancel this appointment and give a chance to true, deserving tribals who are qualified for this work. We want the empowerment of local tribals. Many of them are still languishing in jails for providing food to Naxals out of fear. Why is there no rehabilitation for them?” asked Bajirao Usendi from Gadchiroli.
Mr. Usendi is the leader of a Mahagramsabha, an informal body that plays an advisory role to local gram sabhas in Gadchiroli. Members of the Mahagramsabha include gram sabha members from Naxal-affected areas like Etapalli, Kurkheda, Kurki, etc. The four-page note issued by the Mahagramsabha has expressed strong objection to the University’s decision.
PESA stands for the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996, a landmark law enacted by the Union Government to ensure self-governance for tribal communities living in Fifth Schedule areas.
Bhupati is a dreaded former Maoist whose surrender last year crippled Maoism in Maharashtra. Currently under police supervision in Gadchiroli, he was recently appointed coordinator by Gondwana University to spread awareness among tribal communities about PESA, Forest Rights Act, and other rights of the communities. It is a temporary position.
The Mahagramsabha has issued a memorandum to the Gondwana University, the District Collector, and the Gadchiroli Police Superintendent, calling for the appointment to be revoked.
Temporary appointment
Meanwhile, the University has stated that the appointment is for three months, and that Bhupati will have only clerical responsibility. “He was appointed after due process. Mr. Venugopal will not be given any responsibility to guide the gramsabha or conduct training on anything,” Vice Chancellor of Gondwana University Prashant Bokare said.
However, the appointment notification issued by the University on August 29, which has been perused by The Hindu, clearly stated that the project coordinator was being appointed for integrated gram sabha training programme.
“This appointment is against tribal interests. These very Naxals hid in the jungles, threatened local tribals, and took young girls. Their parents faced attacks, and tribal sarpanchs or local tribal workers whose ideas did not align with the Naxals were brutally murdered. So many tribals have died in Naxal attacks. To this day, those who sheltered Naxals out of fear of their guns are lodged in prisons,” Mr. Usendi said.
The Mahagramsabha demanded to know why local tribals were not given such job opportunities for their empowerment.
Gadchiroli Police Superintendent M. Ramesh did not accept calls despite several attempts. Gadchiroli Collector Avishyant Panda confirmed that a delegation of Mahagramsabha had met him to hand over the memorandum. Gondwana University Vice Chancellor Prashant Bokare said he was on leave due to a death in the family and was not in a position to speak to the media.

The Eiffel Tower has reopened after a one-day strike was called in response to the landmark’s management ordering female staff to keep out of sight at the request of a visiting religious group.
City Hall, which operates the Paris landmark, has apologised for breaching France’s republican principle of equality and ordered a full inquiry.
Workers at the tower walked out on Monday, closing the landmark to visitors, after female colleagues were sidelined and replaced during a visit organised by a Hindu religious group at the weekend.
In a statement, staff said they objected to “professional instructions that led to female employees being sidelined, replaced and made invisible because of their sex” during the visit.
“Some were asked to leave their posts and wait in separate rooms. In some posts, women were replaced by men. All female employees were instructed not to pass through or enter certain areas while the [Hindu] delegation was present,” they said in a statement.
Employees said they were shocked to find themselves in a situation that was “deeply contrary to the values of equality and nondiscrimination”.
“The Eiffel Tower is the symbol of France. We believe it must also be exemplary in the values it promotes and the way it treats staff,” the statement said.
The Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) spiritual movement, whose members made the request in advance of a visit on Saturday, apologised.
“To our knowledge, nobody was refused access to the Eiffel Tower at any moment. Nevertheless, We offer our sincere apologies to anyone who may have been hurt or offended by this situation,” it wrote in a statement.
BAPS is close to India’s ruling Hindu nationalist party, Bharatiya Janata, and was in France to consecrate its first major temple in the country on Sunday.
The public-owned Eiffel Tower operating company (SETE) acknowledged that BAPS had requested that “interactions with women” be limited, and said it should not have accepted these conditions. “They are not in keeping with SETE’s values or the principles of equality between women and men and the neutrality that must guide the organisation of visits to the monument,” it said.
Emmanuel Grégoire, the mayor of Paris, has promised an investigation to “get to the bottom of this as soon as possible”.
He said moving female staff out of sight was unacceptable.
“These are not my values nor those the Eiffel Tower must represent,” he wrote on X.
Ariel Weil, mayor of the Paris Centre district and president of SETE, said he was unaware of the “shocking and unacceptable” conditions afforded the visiting group.
“I confirm again the Eiffel Tower’s commitment to republican values and gender equality,” he said.

Eye donation is said to be one of the most meaningful forms of donation, as a single donor can potentially restore sight to two individuals through corneal transplantation. India has made considerable progress in eye banking; the country currently has 396 functional eye banks, and corneal collections increased from 62,370 in 2022–23 to 69,848 in 2024–25. However, the need for donor tissue substantially exceeds its availability. There are approximately 2 million corneally blind people in our country, but only 40,000 corneal transplants performed per year.
Role of stakeholders
The government has a crucial role in strengthening the eye donation ecosystem through the National Programme for Control of Blindness and Visual Impairment (NPCBVI). Government support includes funding for eye bank infrastructure and equipment, training of ophthalmologists and eye bank technicians, promotion of eye donation, and provision of corneal storage media. Government hospitals can further improve donation rates by establishing Hospital Cornea Retrieval Programmes (HCRP) and integrating eye donation into routine end-of-life counselling.
Non-governmental organisations and service organisations have an equally important role in creating awareness, dispelling myths, encouraging pledges and, most importantly, counselling families at the time of death. Organisations such as eye bank networks, Lions Clubs and other community-based groups can take the message of eye donation to schools, colleges, workplaces and rural communities.
Private eye hospitals and institutions can complement these efforts by establishing or strengthening eye banks, developing efficient corneal retrieval networks, maintaining high standards of tissue evaluation and preservation, and providing advanced corneal transplantation. Recent initiatives such as the expansion of the National Eye Bank at AIIMS, Delhi through partnerships with additional hospitals demonstrate the value of collaborative retrieval networks.
Building strong PPPs
Ultimately, the future of eye donation in India lies in a strong public–private–NGO partnership. Awareness must translate into timely family consent, consent into retrieval, and retrieved tissue into high-quality transplantation. Strengthening this entire chain will be essential to bring down the burden of corneal blindness and make the gift of sight a reality for many more Indians.
The goal is clear: to transform the gift of eye donation into the gift of sight. Every donated cornea carries a legacy of compassion—allowing one person’s life to bring light into another’s.
(Dr. Mohan Rajan is chairman and medical director and Dr. Sujatha Mohan is executive medical director, of Rajan Eye Care Hospital. drmohanrajan@gmail.com)

People are not happy about Flock Safety’s automated license plate readers and the cops that allegedly misuse them. If you’re one of those ALPR-haters, you can now take out your rage in the video game Grand Theft Auto V by installing Grand Theft Automated License Plate Reader, a mod built by artist Morry Kolman.
The mod installs 235 Flock cameras around the fictional Los Santos, a riff on the real-life city of Los Angeles. Players can smash and shoot down the cameras and get paid $600 for each one they destroy, which Kolman priced based on a teardown of a Flock Falcon Flex Camera by the Iowa-based civil liberties group Eyes Off of Cedar Rapids. The in-game cameras log every time a player destroys and drives by one, and players can render a photo album of their interactions.
In real life, vigilantes have allegedly wrecked Flock cameras in their communities using spray-paint, saws, bullets, and even flaming projectiles. An NPR analysis found that Flock cameras have been vandalized in at least 36 states.
“GTPLR is not an endorsement of the activities that it allows in the game in the same way that GTA is not an endorsement of the activities that are allowed in the game,” says Kolman, referring to the fact that GTA is largely about doing fictional crimes. “But I think there is a public appetite for some kind of cathartic release against these machines.”
In addition to being fun objects to destroy, the GTA cameras also operate as an extension of the police in-game. Passing by one of the 235 cameras while being chased by the cops prolongs the game’s cooldown period. Because of how dense the cameras are in some areas, it can make the game impossible to play.
There’s also a 5 percent chance that the cameras will trigger a random police response even if the player isn’t doing anything wrong, which Kolman says was inspired by news reports about innocent people being held at gunpoint because of ALPR errors.
“There are violent responses and really dangerous situations that are created by these cameras and their inaccuracies,” says Kolman.
Flock did not immediately respond to a request for comment for this story.
GTA V has been around for over a decade, and a rich modding community has built up around it (WIRED covered one back in 2015.) The long-awaited sequel, Grand Theft Auto VI, is slated to come out in November and will be set in a fictional version of Miami called Vice City.
Kolman doesn’t have specific plans to build a version of GTALPR for that, joking, “We'll probably wait to see what the people of Vice City and their local government have already installed around their map.”
In real-life LA, the Los Angeles Police Department suspended its use of Flock cameras this summer following a recommendation from the LAPD’s inspector general. The tide is turning in other places too—governors in both Texas and Florida recently took steps to curtail the use of Flock cameras in their respective states, and across the US, there were 131 Flock contract terminations in August alone, according to the anti-surveillance advocacy group Secure Justice.
For all the fun that fake-smashing surveillance cameras can be, Kolman seriously hopes that players can feel the “insidiousness and inescapability of the surveillance” through GTALPR.
“I know that you could read a thousand articles about why surveillance is bad and why Flock is horrible,” says Kolman. “Or I could make you feel how pervasive these Flock cameras are by having you try to drive around the map of Los Santos.”

Norway to bid farewell to King Harald V with funeral attended by royalty, dignitaries
Norway will bid its final farewell to King Harald V with a funeral paying tribute to the 35-year reign of the popular monarch who died on Aug. 28, aged 89
OSLO, Norway -- Norway will bid its final farewell to King Harald V on Wednesday with a funeral attended by royalty and leaders from across Europe and beyond, who will pay tribute to the popular monarch's 35-year reign.
Harald, who died on Aug. 28 aged 89, was Europe’s oldest monarch and had modernized the royal house, but refused to follow in the footsteps of other aging monarchs who have abdicated in recent times. His son immediately became King Haakon VIII and last week pledged an oath of allegiance to Norway's constitution in parliament.
On Wednesday, the coffin will be taken from the royal palace to Oslo Cathedral in a procession, followed by Haakon, other senior Norwegian royals, foreign guests and representatives of Norway’s parliament and others.
Ahead of the funeral, Norwegians have waited patiently to file past Harald's coffin as it lay in state in the chapel of the royal palace in Oslo. The queue was seven hours long at one point over the weekend.
Large crowds are expected in the capital for the funeral. The downtown area will be closed to vehicles and electric scooters, and police have instructed people not to bring bicycles, umbrellas or sharp objects. Large screens have been set up for people to watch the ceremony.
Among the guests expected to attend are the monarchs of Sweden, Denmark, Spain, the Netherlands, Belgium and Jordan. The heir to the British throne, Prince William, is also expected, as is Crown Prince Akishino of Japan. Presidents from a range of European countries will join them.
A minute's silence will be held across Norway at the start of the funeral ceremony. Eulogies will be delivered by Norway's parliament speaker and prime minister, and there will be a candle-lighting ceremony with representatives of different faiths.
After the funeral, Harald's coffin will be taken in a procession to the palace chapel at Akershus Castle, where the late king's ancestors are buried. After a private ceremony for the Norwegian royals, who will be joined by some of the foreign guests and senior Norwegian officials, it will be lowered into the crypt.
Norway’s monarchy traces its origins to King Harald Fairhair in the ninth century. When Norway regained its independence from Sweden in 1905, three-quarters of voters in a national plebiscite approved restoring the monarchy.
Today, the throne's role is largely symbolic and power lies with the elected government and parliament, but the Norwegian royal family retains a role in promoting the wealthy Scandinavian nation around the world.

2028 Volvo XC40 First Look: Hello new tech, goodbye EV
Volvo refreshed the XC40, but it's sadly doing away with the all-electric EX40 in the US.
Volvo is a brand traditionally known for its safety-minded station wagons and the Labrador Retrievers contained within, but lately it has well and truly embraced the SUV wave. While its midsize offering, the XC60, is its primary sales winner in the United States, the compact XC40 is the brand's third-best-selling model here, and second-highest internaionally.
The current-generation XC40 dates back to 2017, joined by the all-electric XC40 Recharge in 2019, which was rechristened in 2024 to become the EX40 to keep up with the company's evolving all-electric nomenclature. That branding includes the EX30, EX60, and the EX90.
For the 2028 model year, both the EX40 and XC40 are getting a major visual refresh plus an injection of extra tech into the software interface and active safety systems. That's the good news. The bad news? Starting in 2028, we'll only get half of that pairing.
A new look
The current-generation XC40 got a slight refresh in 2022, but looking back, you'd be forgiven for having a hard time telling the two versions apart, with a slightly reshaped nose and revised headlights.
For 2028, the revisions are a bit more significant, even if the overall shape of the car again remains largely the same. The front, though, is significantly revised. Where the front bumper formerly presented a face with numerous cut-outs and scalloped sections, now everything is far simpler.
It's a distinctly more modern look highlighted by the revised headlights. Yes, Volvo's trademark Thor's hammer design remains, but the various other lighting elements are now largely hidden, creating a stark effect.
Simpler designs
The hood and fenders have likewise been resculpted, and things out back have changed to match the revised front end, again all resulting in a cleaner design throughout. Cast a shadow over the new XC40, and you won't spot the differences, but in the daylight the net result is a distinctly more modern-looking SUV.
Over on the electric EX40, that machine gets all the same revisions. That means these two SUVs are nigh indistinguishable when sitting next to each other. Yes, the badging on the back is different, of course, but the bigger tell is the grille on the revised nose. The EX40's grille is a flat, body-colored panel, while the XC40's now contains an array of diagonal slashes meant to accentuate the Volvo logo and the arrow it's forever firing up and to the right.
New tech
Volvo retooled the interiors of the EX40 and XC40 as well, but the changes are even more subtle. The most notable is a new, larger screen that's been somewhat crudely grafted atop the center of the dashboard. Where the old display was nicely recessed between the tall central vents, fitting nicely in a recess in the dash, the new one stands outward, taller than the dash.
It's not a bad look, and the result is 11.2 inches of display real estate, up from the 9 inches the XC40 had before. The software running behind that screen has been updated as well, the latest flavor of Android Automotive that brings Google's Gemini to the party.
Gemini can handle changes to vehicle settings, control the infotainment experience and do everything else you'd expect your friendly local agentic instance to do — for better or worse. That means not only finding nearby restaurants but also getting summaries of their gluten-free offerings or vegetarian fare. Or, you can get route suggestions when you have a little extra time to kill and want to see some scenery on the way.
None of that, though, is exactly new. Indeed, Volvo added Gemini to most of its models earlier this year. Thankfully, the XC40's interior was already among the better-looking and feeling spaces in this segment, and that's still the case, now just with a bigger screen and some updated ambient lighting as well.
Enhanced safety
The biggest changes on the new EX40 and XC40 might be under the skin — or in some cases embedded within it. Volvo has outfitted these SUVs with an improved sensing package, including high-res cameras looking in every direction, ultrasonic sensors in the bumpers and updated radar.
This has a few immediate benefits, including the availability of a detailed, 3D view of the car that was previously restricted to Volvo's bigger, more expensive models. This also enables an automated lane-change feature in the Pilot Assist active safety system, which still includes an advanced, hands-on lane-keep system and adaptive cruise.
Those features are also said to be improved, with everything controlled by an updated central safety controller that has more processing power than before and is over-the-air updatable, meaning more advanced driver assistance features could be added down the road.
No details on which features might be coming and when, but don't hold your breath on hands-off driver systems like BMW's Highway Assistant or Tesla's Full Self-Driving. Volvo CEO Håkan Samuelsson has made it very clear that the company is in no rush to let drivers take their hands off the wheel.
Adios EX40
The final update is probably the saddest: While Volvo is updating both the EX40 and XC40 internationally, the United States will not be getting the updated battery-electric version. We'll only get the XC40 in B5 trim.
That means a 2.0-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine that outputs 247 horsepower and 266 pound-feet of torque. It has an eight-speed automatic transmission and a small electric motor to help deliver a combined 27 mpg fuel efficiency.
The all-electric EX40 will live on internationally. Why not domestically? You can surely blame some combination of tepid sales and its foreign manufacture. That's a shame, especially since the smaller EX30 has also left American shores, but at least Volvo hasn't suffered Polestar's fate.
Wrap-up
So the EX40's days are numbered, with that model turning into a pumpkin after the current inventory is depleted. But the XC40 lives on with its updated face and refreshed sensor package. As a 2028 model, though, you'll have to wait a bit to get one. Volvo says it won't start hitting dealerships until sometime early next year, with pricing to be revealed sometime closer to arrival.

The Wedding Photographer of Darfur
Mohammed, a photographer from Darfur, was forced to flee the violence in el-Fasher and now lives in Tawila, a refuge for thousands displaced by the conflict in Sudan.
For years, he documented Sudan's wars, capturing scenes of displacement, loss, and survival. Today, his lens is focused on something very different, couples, families and communities celebrating best days they have not had in a long times.

Mirzapur The Movie has rocked the box office and opened more than expectations. After collecting Rs. 24.47 crores on day 1, it went on to collect Rs. 31.30 crores and Rs. 35.18 crores on Saturday and Sunday respectively. Hence, it had a weekend of Rs. 90.95 crores. We spoke to trade experts about its box office performance and a lot more.
Trade experts AMAZED by Mirzapur The Movie’s box office performance: “It’s a case study”; predict a new trend: “At least 10 films will be made based on web series”
Trade veteran Taran Adarsh said, “I don’t think even the producers imagined that the weekend would be close to Rs. 100 crores. People in the industry did expect the film to open well as it’s an action masala fare. It was also believed that it would excel in mass pockets. However, it has performed exceptionally across the board. From the advance booking itself, it was evident that it was going to take a flying start. From that point onwards, right until the end of the weekend, the film continued to surprise.”
He added, “It is an eye-opener as it doesn’t have a conventional A-lister or top star. Secondly, for a film based on a web series to do such massive numbers at the box office is a rarity. We have often heard people say after watching certain films, ‘This film should have been released directly on OTT’ or ‘This looks like an OTT film’. But now, these OTT characters have come to the big screen and done such roaring business!”
Trade analyst Atul Mohan commented, “This is the khasiyat of box office. You never know what would work and what won’t. At times, we feel that a certain film will be a sure-shot hit, and it fails. Then some films release with minimal or zero expectations, and they surprise. Mirzapur has proved that you don’t need any stars. If you have a brand value and position it well, it can click big time.”
He continued, “When we discuss the best shows on OTT, Mirzapur always gets mentioned. The makers knew that brand toh hai, ek chance le sakte hain. The characters are popular, especially in the Northern belt. Also, when your brand is a star, you don’t need a famous actor.”
Distributor and exhibitor Raj Bansal confessed, “I was expecting an opening of Rs. 20-22 crores and a weekend of Rs. 75 crores. At the most, I thought it’ll do Rs. 80 crores if the film enjoyed positive reports. However, it has surpassed all expectations and did more than Rs. 90 crores in 3 days. It has even crossed Awarapan 2’s opening weekend numbers.”
Girish Johar, producer and film business analyst, remarked, “The good part is that the theatrical business is up and the film is drawing these kinds of numbers without any so-called A-listers. It is purely because of the resonance the audience has with the web series. The marketing was also done accordingly, and they delivered in terms of content as well, as evident from the reports. Hence, the industry is very pleasantly surprised. I take this as a learning, and it makes it clear that stars are not the only deciding factor at the box office. The story, presentation and content matter just as much.”
A case study
All experts agreed that Mirzapur is now a case study. Taran Adarsh explained, “Audience ki soch bahut alag hai. Hum kuch aur sochte hain aur audience kuch aur. The most surprising part is that in its 25 years’ journey, Excel Entertainment has produced some of the biggest films with Shah Rukh Khan, Aamir Khan, Akshay Kumar, Hrithik Roshan, etc. But those films did not get the kind of numbers that this film got. Hence, this film is a case study for everybody in the industry.”
He continued, “You don’t need stars or big names to attract footfalls or have house-full boards. And most importantly, people are back in theatres in a big way. That’s a huge plus. There was a belief that ‘Tickets are so expensive. Theatre mein kaun jaayega?’. But look at the business over the weekend of Mirzapur The Movie as well as Hanuman Ansh. Moreover, both films belong to diverse profiles. Yet, both did roaring business.”
They also said that it’ll give rise to a new trend. Atul Mohan predicted, “Makers of many more OTT shows will also try to make films.” Taran Adarsh agreed, “I am sure a lot of people must be thinking along those lines (laughs). All I can say is that not every film can be a Mirzapur and not every devotional film can be Hanuman Ansh. What’s important is that there’s a new revenue model now. Earlier, it was believed that one should make conventional films. But this shows that the audience is ready to try something different.”
Raj Bansal sighed, “This is very common in our industry. Once something works, toh line lag jaati hai. This will be no exception. At least 10 films will be made based on web series, whether or not they are successful. This would be considered the easy route to take.”
Girish Johar cautioned, “I don’t want people to do bhedchaal kind of stuff. Makers should keep in mind what the audiences actually want rather than making a film on some show that probably has done well.”

Apple's new iPhone Duo costs more in Canada, but not because of tariffs
Starting price for foldable phone, revealed on Wednesday, is almost 10% more than in the U.S.
Canadians are used to seeing higher prices than what our neighbours in the U.S., but the price gap for the latest iPhone has caused some double takes.
The iPhone Duo, Apple's new foldable phone revealed Wednesday, is retailing for prices ranging from $2,999 to $4,799 in Canada, before tax.
In the U.S., prices start at $1,999 US, which works out as $2,760 — meaning Canadians will have to pay almost 10 per cent more for the cheapest version.
The sticker shock drew jeers and jokes on a Canadian Reddit forum, with one user saying anyone who spends that much on a phone should have to take a financial literacy class.
"You used to be able to buy a car for that amount," another wrote.
University of Toronto economics professor Joseph Steinberg says the price bump likely signals that Apple recognized the subset of the Canadian population that would buy a "super-premium product" like the Duo is "less price sensitive" relative to American consumers, "and therefore they can get away with jacking up the margin a little bit more."
He notes that it's not unusual for electronics and other products to be more expensive in Canada.
"This one just stands out because of how darn expensive this phone is, I think, more than anything," Steinberg said.
It's not tariffs: profs
Some have speculated that Canada's new retaliatory tariffs on U.S. products would raise iPhone prices, but experts told CBC News that is not a factor in this case.
While the list of U.S. products tariffed at 50 per cent includes smartphones, Steinberg says Canada does not actually import the devices from the U.S. in any meaningful quantity.
Additionally, Canada's tariffs do not apply to the iPhone Duo because the phones are built in China and are therefore treated as a product originating in China and not the U.S., he says.
"What matters for whether a tariff is applied is where the project originates from, not where it last crossed the border into Canada from," he added.
Canada's counter-tariffs on U.S. products came into effect early Tuesday, prompting Washington to escalate the countries' trade dispute by banning certain goods imported from Canada and introducing more tariffs of its own later that day.
Microchip shortage raising prices
Werner Antweiler, chair in international trade policy at the University of British Columbia, says virtually all electronics Canadians buy come from Asia, and include components made around the world.
He says the reason smartphone prices are rising in general is because of the global microchip shortage caused by the AI boom and the rapid spread of data centres, creating a "crazy demand" that is driving up manufacturing prices.
Antweiler says he's surprised to see Apple specifically raise its prices more for Canadian consumers, though he notes it's not an uncommon practice for U.S. companies.
"Price discrimination is not unusual, and that can be in the magnitude of 10 to 15 per cent, because that is typically what the Canadian market will pay more," he said, adding that's largely because Canada is a smaller market than the U.S.
CBC News has contacted Apple for comment but has not heard back.
Apple CEO John Ternus led the unveiling of the iPhone Duo on Wednesday, which marked a major change to the company's flagship product in his first event since taking the leadership role.
Pre-orders for the Duo begin on Oct. 17 and the phone will be available Oct. 23.

PM-Xi Jinping bilateral likely at BRICS, first in India since 2020 Galwan clash
Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to arrive in New Delhi on Saturday for the BRICS Summit, where he is likely to hold his first bilateral meeting with PM Narendra Modi since the 2020 Galwan Valley clash.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi is likely to hold a bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi on September 12, marking the first face-to-face bilateral talks between the two leaders since the deadly Galwan Valley clash of 2020.
The meeting is expected to be closely watched as India and China attempt to consolidate a cautious thaw in ties after years of military tensions, diplomatic estrangement and a sharp deterioration in economic engagement.
Xi is scheduled to arrive in New Delhi on Saturday for the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit, which India will host on September 12 and 13. This will also mark his first visit to India in seven years and his first since the border crisis. New Delhi and Beijing are yet to issue a formal statement on the high-stakes meeting.
The two leaders recently shared the stage at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Kyrgyzstan’s Bishkek, where they shook hands, but did not hold a formal bilateral meeting.

Hanuman Ansh has continued its impressive run at the box office even after spending more than a month in theatres. The Shobhinaw Satyaa and Chandan Anand-starrer, which had a slow start, has turned into a surprise blockbuster as its collections picked up in the following weeks. According to Sacnilk, the film earned Rs 10.25 crore net in India on Day 34. The collection came from 7,810 shows, with the film recording an overall occupancy of 35 per cent.
The Day 34 collection marks a 4.7 per cent drop from the previous day. Hanuman Ansh had earned Rs 10.75 crore on Day 33. With the latest earnings added, the film's India net collection has climbed to Rs 153.13 crore, while its India gross collection stands at Rs 180.95 crore. The film has also officially crossed the Rs 150 crore milestone in India net collections.
Hanuman Ansh's slow start and strong turnaround
Unlike its current box office performance, Hanuman Ansh opened to a rather muted response. The film collected just Rs 10 lakh on its opening Friday, with 355 shows and 10 per cent occupancy.
Its second week remained equally subdued, contributing only Rs 40 lakh. However, the film witnessed a major turnaround in its third week, when it collected Rs 10.40 crore.
The fourth week further strengthened its momentum. The film began the week with Rs 6.25 crore on Friday from 2,829 shows at 52 per cent occupancy. Saturday saw the collection rise to Rs 9.25 crore from 4,137 shows at 53 per cent occupancy. On Sunday, it reached its fourth-week peak with Rs 12.75 crore, registering 55 per cent occupancy across 5,363 shows.
The film collected Rs 5.50 crore on Monday from 6,587 shows at 22 per cent occupancy, followed by Rs 8.50 crore on Tuesday from 7,008 shows at 46 per cent occupancy.
Hanuman Ansh entered its fifth week on a strong note, earning Rs 10 crore on Friday from 5,055 shows at 47 per cent occupancy. Saturday brought in Rs 16.50 crore from 6,055 shows, with occupancy rising to 62 per cent. The film then recorded another jump on Sunday, collecting Rs 22.75 crore from 7,077 shows at 73 per cent occupancy. It followed this with Rs 10 crore on Monday from 7,343 shows at 36 per cent occupancy.
Story and making of Hanuman Ansh
Hanuman Ansh is a biographical devotional drama written, directed and produced by Dr Vishal Chaturvedi. The film is the first instalment of a planned trilogy based on his book Divine Detour: That Changed My Life, which chronicles the life of Neem Karoli Baba.

The Asian Games began in Japan on Thursday when Qatar beat Iran in the men’s basketball opening group game, the first action in the continental multi-sport showpiece that has more participants than the Olympics.
Over 17,000 athletes and officials are expected to take part in 43 sports at the Nagoya-Aichi Games — which do not officially start until the opening ceremony on September 19 and will run until October 4.
Several events, such as basketball, football, cricket, hockey and modern pentathlon, will get underway before the opening ceremony.
Qatar held off a comeback from Iran to win its Group B encounter 59-35 at the Aichi International Arena in Nagoya in the first match of a men’s basketball competition that will hold medal finals on September 20, the day after the opening ceremony.
Los Angeles 2028 Olympics qualifying spots are up for grabs in several sports at the Asian Games, which are returning to Japan for the first time since 1994.
Organisers hope the athletes will have a “unique experience” staying in eye-catching accommodation ranging from a cruise liner and wooden containers to standard hotel rooms.
Officials are confident that the plan will not be affected by Japan’s typhoon season, which is usually in full swing in September-October.
Weather has already caused disruptions, with record rainfall on Tuesday forcing hundreds of athletes briefly to evacuate their accommodation.
Rainwater also leaked into some competition venues, with more wet weather forecast for the coming days.
Among those in action at the Games will be Philippine tennis sensation Alexandra Eala and a pair of world-class teenage talents in 15-year-old Indian cricketer Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and 13-year-old Chinese swimmer Yu Zidi.

Ola Electric’s FY26 annual report disclosed another suspected employee fraud at its wholly owned subsidiary Ola Electric Technologies Pvt Ltd (OET), with auditors reporting two such offences involving more than ₹1 Cr. According to OET’s secretarial audit report, the statutory auditors reported the two suspected employee frauds to the central government through e-form ADT-4 filings dated July 9, 2025, and June 4, 2026. While one suspected fraud was disclosed in Ola Electric’s FY25 annual report, the filing made in June 2026 appears to relate to a second case. However, the latest annual report did not disclose the employees involved, the nature of the suspected frauds, or the precise amount involved in either case. It is also unclear whether the “amount exceeding ₹1 Cr” refers to each offence or the two cases collectively. Queries sent to Ola Electric remained unanswered at the time of publishing. The story will be updated upon receiving a response. Inventory Weakness Persists The disclosure comes amid continuing concerns around internal controls at Ola Electric. Its statutory auditors issued a qualified opinion on the group’s internal financial controls, citing a material weakness related to the physical verification of finished goods and raw materials at OET’s plant and stores. As of March 31, 2026, the group had ₹251 Cr worth of raw materials and finished goods covered by the audit matter. Of this, inventory worth ₹153 Cr had not been physically verified during FY26 or subsequently up to the date of the consolidated financial statements. The issue echoes FY25, when auditors had flagged a similar weakness involving ₹362 Cr worth of electric two-wheelers and spare parts that had not been physically verified at stores and state distribution centres. Ola Electric had attributed the FY25 lapse to a temporary realignment of inventory processes under Project Lakshya and said it had found no financial impact or inventory misplacement. The company similarly described the FY26 observation as an isolated case. It said a redesign of its network operations in Q4 FY26 temporarily disrupted inventory processes, preventing management from undertaking physical verification at the end of the year. However, Ola Electric said its ERP system did not show any discrepancy and that physical verification was conducted before and after the network redesign. The company appointed TRC Corporate Consulting as its external internal auditor after the end of FY26. During the fiscal year, Ola Electric relied on internal resources to monitor and review its controls and processes. Workforce Churn Surges Ola Electric also reported a sharp increase in employee turnover during FY26. The turnover rate among permanent employees rose to 60% from 54% in FY25, while that among permanent workers surged to 105% from 29%. The company attributed the higher rate primarily to increased attrition among permanent workers and said the vacant positions would be filled or appointments made afresh. The increase followed multiple rounds of job cuts at Ola Electric. The company reportedly cut around 500 jobs in 2024, followed by more than 1,000 layoffs in March 2025. In January 2026, Ola Electric announced another restructuring exercise that was expected to impact around 5% of its workforce as it increased automation across its front-end operations. The restructuring formed part of Ola Electric’s attempt to move away from rapid expansion and build a leaner operating model following a weak fiscal year. The company’s revenue from operations halved to ₹2,253 Cr in FY26 from ₹4,514 Cr in the previous fiscal year. Meanwhile, net loss narrowed 19.5% to ₹1,833 Cr from ₹2,276 Cr in FY25. The revenue decline came as Ola Electric’s deliveries fell to 1.74 Lakh units in FY26 from 3.59 Lakh units in FY25. During the year, the company also continued to face criticism over delivery timelines, after-sales service, and regulatory issues. Ola Electric called FY26 a “year of structural reset”, during which it rationalised its retail network, cut costs, strengthened service operations, and focused on improving unit economics. More recently, the company opened its sales and service network to dealer partners, marking a shift from its earlier company-owned retail model. It is targeting more than 500 dealerships over the next few quarters, while its company-owned outlets will transition into product experience centres. Ola Electric also raised ₹780.2 Cr through a QIP in June. Earlier this month, its board approved another fundraise of up to ₹1,500 Cr, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. Meanwhile, the company is expanding its battery cell business. It has “largely” completed the installation required for its 6 GWh cell manufacturing platform. In August, it launched the S1Z, its first escooter range powered by the company’s Bharat Cell LFP technology.

Russell hindered or just Antonelli brilliance? - F1 Q&A
- Published
Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli climbed from 19th on the grid to win the Italian Grand Prix - his home race - in one of the great Formula 1 drives.
Antonelli extended his lead at the top of the drivers' standings to 66 points over team-mate George Russell.
Max Verstappen, in the Red Bull, finished third to complete the podium at Monza.
BBC Sport F1 correspondent Andrew Benson answers your latest questions before round 14 of the 2026 season in Madrid, Spain.
- Antonelli 'walks over water' for win that will go down in F1 folklore 
  - Published1 day ago
Why wasn't George Russell given the opportunity by Mercedes to pit under the virtual safety car in the Italian Grand Prix? I know he had the hard tyres on, but as the lead driver on track should he not have been at least given the choice? - Tom
In hindsight, it would be easy to think there would be some controversy around the decisions that were taken when the virtual safety car was called mid-race at the Italian Grand Prix.
In reality, though, there was not any.
At the time, George Russell was leading the race on the hard tyre and Kimi Antonelli was second on the medium, a few laps after the Mercedes drivers had been advised to call off their 'yo-yo' scrapping to allow them to optimise their pace and build a gap to Max Verstappen's Red Bull.
Without a VSC, the question was whether the mediums on Antonelli's car would last to the end - probably not - and what Mercedes would do about that.
With or without the VSC, the race result was up in the air.
The VSC changed the complexion of the race, but Russell, who had fitted hards at the red flag with the express intention of going to the end, said he had given no thought to changing tyres at the time.
"I didn't," he said. "I actually thought the guys behind me were going to stay out as well. But I'm sure the team were quite nervous on the pit wall watching our battle and were probably quite happy to send us on different strategies.
"And of course, when we had Max in the mix as well, from a team perspective, you're covering off both scenarios.
"If either of us were to pit, it was going to be Kimi. And that's why I was just a little bit annoyed with the timing of that VSC because I think it would have been tough for those guys on the medium to have competed with anybody on the hard tyre. But it takes nothing away from Kimi's drive."
At the time, Mercedes' strategy computers were saying staying out was the best option.
Team principal Toto Wolff said: "We didn't know what was the better strategy. At that stage, the system said that the one-stop comes out ahead. That two-stop was coming close to the end, but didn't catch it. That's what the software said."
All of which goes to underline the main takeaway - the sublime quality of Antonelli's drive.
He made remarkable progress up through the field from 19th on the grid, wasting no time in picking off cars in front, minimising any loss from overtaking to his overall race time.
He made this look easy, but as many other drivers proved at Monza on Sunday, overtaking another car of similar performance and immediately pulling away was anything but.
This was a performance for the ages - like Lewis Hamilton in Brazil in 2021, Max Verstappen in Brazil in 2024 or 2025, or Fernando Alonso in Valencia in 2012.
McLaren team principal Andrea Stella, who knows a thing or two about this sort of performance having worked with Michael Schumacher and Alonso, said: "While he had a very competitive car, we have to say that he beat a team-mate starting second on the grid.
"It's a very special day, very important for his championship. But for his career and for the fans, motorsport in general, this will be an iconic day. This will be remembered in the years to come."
Is Charles Leclerc's tendency to crash out of races starting to become a problem both for him and Ferrari? - Nathan
Charles Leclerc certainly did not have his best day in Monza on Sunday.
He was arguably too aggressive with Lewis Hamilton at the first chicane on the first lap, forcing his team-mate into the gravel and dropping him to 10th, and crashed out a lap later.
By then, he had also been passed by Max Verstappen, and his accident at Parabolica seemed to be influenced by the fact he was slightly wide into, through and out of the corner because he was defending an attack from McLaren's Oscar Piastri, although Leclerc himself said he thought that was not the cause of his crash.
"I wouldn't say that this is the issue," he said. "From lap one to lap two, I had a bit of a difference in power delivery. We'll look into it, but I don't want to comment too much before checking the data and confirming it 100%."
Having said that, does the allegation that Leclerc has a "tendency to crash out of races" stand up?
He has done it twice so far this year - the previous time was in Monaco, when he lost control at a restart on the broken track surface at Anthony Noghes.
But, unless I've missed something, you have to go back nearly three years to the one before that, when he retired with car damage after an incident-packed race at Zandvoort in 2023.
In that period, for comparison, Hamilton has done the same thing four times - Brazil and Netherlands last year, Austin in 2024 and Qatar in 2023.
Ferrari clearly have some things to sort out, however, in terms of their operations and general approach.
Hamilton is not happy about the way the team have effectively disregarded his - albeit slim - title hopes this year in favour of driver equality, and he said after dropping more points to Antonelli on Sunday that it was "far too late for those decisions to come".
The incident between Leclerc and Hamilton on lap one took place in the context of Hamilton saying after qualifying they had to "work as a team to try and topple" Mercedes.
Leclerc said of the first-corner incident: "I don't really know who is forcing that narrative that we are one against the other. I mean, honestly, Zandvoort there was way too many talks already.
"Here it's true, though, that we went too far. Lewis in Turn One, then Turn Two, I tried to do the tightest corner possible, but that was just not enough and doing it here is not good."
Hamilton was not impressed by the suggestion he had done anything wrong at Turn One.
When those remarks were put to Hamilton, he said: "He said what? I was ahead in Turn Two. By the ethics, I was ahead. There was no 'we' in it."
He added: "I don't race dirty. I've always raced clean and fairly and always left space."
Team boss Frederic Vasseur, who said he would talk to the drivers before discussing this in the media, has some smoothing out to do before this weekend's race in Madrid.
Aston Martin have had their major upgrades but were right at the back of the grid again in Monza. Have the upgrades just failed? - Colin
Aston Martin had a major car upgrade in Hungary two races ago, and a "spec two" Honda engine at the race before Italy in Zandvoort, on either side of the summer break.
There is no question the car upgrade worked. What was effectively an all-new car, apart from the rear suspension and gearbox, cut lap times by about two seconds.
Fernando Alonso made it into the second part of qualifying for the first time all year in Hungary, and drove an outstanding race to finish ninth on merit in the Netherlands, on a one-stop strategy, holding at arm's length the faster Alpine of Pierre Gasly and Racing Bull of Yuki Tsunoda in the final stint.
More upgrades are expected, in the form of a weight reduction around the gearbox, for either Madrid this weekend or Azerbaijan.
The Honda engine upgrade that made its debut in Zandvoort has been less impressive, which is why Aston Martin found themselves at the back again on the power-sensitive Monza track.
Trackside general manager and chief engineer Shintaro Orihara says Honda "observed a step forward in terms of performance from our metrics".
But if there has been one, it is small. Drivability of the spec two in Zandvoort was noticeably worse, too, although it had made a step forward in Italy.
The Aston Martin car seems to be a midfield-level chassis now, somewhere around the borderline of getting into the final part of qualifying, depending on circuit layout, if it had a competitive engine.
And on the chassis side, the team have a sense of direction that gives them confidence they can make another step next season.
With Honda, which still has comfortably the worst engine in F1, the upgrade has been less reassuring.
What is the new Madring circuit in Spain like in terms of power compared to all the previously visited circuits? Who is it expected to suit most of all? - Andrew
The Madrid circuit which makes its debut this weekend has been built from scratch.
The circuit layout has lots of corners, and it is expected to have a low power sensitivity, around the level of Zandvoort.
Medium-speed corners predominate. And overtaking is expected to be difficult - again, like Zandvoort, or even Hungary.
Given Lando Norris took dominant wins in the Netherlands and Hungary, some teams believe McLaren might be favourites heading into this weekend, but McLaren themselves are not so sure.
Hungary and Zandvoort have long-duration corners, where the McLaren excels. But the Madring corners are generally short duration, the exception being the long, banked Monumental, which is expected to be flat out.
McLaren team principal Andrea Stella said after the race in Monza on Sunday: "We still think that tracks like Baku and Madrid, where you have to be very precise with the trajectory, short corners, maybe they don't play to the best of our car.
"Yet, we have to say that in Zandvoort and Hungary we were in position to win races and here, while we were not, we know that it's a special race.
"Drag will be less important in Madrid. There is a much higher density of corners. We will definitely give it a go."
New tracks always throw up surprises. So, in short, while one can speculate about car and circuit characteristics all one wants, no one will actually know until qualifying on Saturday.

A video (here & here) is being shared on social media claiming that it shows a group of people reciting the Quran on a hilltop in Nepal during rescue operations amid the recent flash floods that occurred on 26 August 2026. Let’s verify the claim made in the post.
Claim: Video showing a group of people reciting the Quran in Nepal during August 2026 Nepal flood rescue operations.
Fact: The video is unrelated to the 2026 Nepal flood rescue operations. It shows local villagers reciting the Quran during a massive search effort in Kyrgyzstan for a 6-year-old boy who was swept away by a river following a tragic car accident. Hence, the claim made in the post is FALSE.
A reverse image search of the keyframes extracted from the viral video led to the same video (archive) uploaded on 25 June 2026 by a Kyrgyzstan-based Instagram page, two months prior to the Nepal tragedy. Additional footage posted by the same account indicates that the viral video is related to a rescue operation in Kyrgyzstan.
According to the media reports (here, here & here), on 23 June 2026, a passenger car fell off a cliff into a river in the Kegety Gorge in Kyrgyzstan’s Chuy region. While the adults and three children managed to escape, two children remained trapped. Rescuers initially recovered the body of a 12-year-old girl, while a 6-year-old boy was swept away by the strong current. The Ministry of Emergency Situations (MES) conducted an active, round-the-clock search operation.
The effort lasted for nearly four days and was joined by local and international volunteers. Reports indicated that local Muslim leaders recited the Quran and prayed for the safe return of the child. The operation concluded on 26 June 2026, when the boy’s body was recovered. Moreover, the viral video shows one of the rescue personnel wearing a chest badge belonging to the Ministry of Emergency Situations (MES) of Kyrgyzstan.
To sum it up, an unrelated video from Kyrgyzstan is being falsely shared as visuals of people reciting the Quran during rescue operations for the August 2026 Nepal floods.

For years, a claim has circulated online that MI5, the U.K.'s internal and domestic security agency, used Boy Scouts as messengers during World War I but replaced them with Girl Guides because the Boy Scouts were too loud and less reliable.
Girl Guides are a similar organization to the Girl Scouts in the United States.
For example, one Instagram profile posted a graphic featuring text that reads (archived), "The Boy Scouts were too noisy for British intelligence, so MI5 trusted its secret messages to teenage Girl Guides instead."
Other iterations of the claim have previously circulated on X, Facebook, Bluesky and Reddit.
According to an MI5 report about its "Organisation and Administration" between 1900 and 1919, the agency employed Boy Scouts to carry messages between officers starting in October 1914. However, the agency found the boys "very troublesome" because they would get into "mischief" during downtime on the job (Page 40) and instead hired Girl Guides, who proved more "amenable" than the boys (Page 41).
In a speech in October 2009, Jonathan Evans, who was the agency's director general at the time, described those same Boy Scout messengers as "feckless and noisy" and the Girl Guide replacements as "more reliable."
Given b
The MI5 report that mentions Girl Guides working for the agency is dated 1921 (Page 3). It is unclear when the agency released the report to the U.K.'s National Archives.
The section about Boy Scouts and Girl Guides says the agency sought out Boy Scouts because it needed messengers for in-house communication. However, the report adds (Page 40-41):
Boys were, however, found to be very troublesome. The considerable periods of inactivity which fell to their share usually resulted in their getting into mischief. When, therefore, the system of employing boys as coast watchers was introduced by the Admiralty, the boys employed by M.0.5. were advised to take up this work; outdoor work being much more fitted to their energy. Arrangements were then made to replace the Boy Scouts with Girl Guides and the results were most satisfactory. The girls proved more amenable and their methods of getting into mischief were on the whole less distressing to those who had to deal with them than were those of the boys.
MI5 was called M.O.5 until 1916.
According to the report, Girl Guides worked in the agency after September 1915 until January 1920 (Page 41).
Girl Guides in the U.K. commemorated the guides that worked for MI5 with a custom badge in 2023. The Girl Guides website says 90 guides, aged 14 to 16 years old, worked for the agency during World War I.
In "How the Girl Guides Won the War: An Extraordinary True Story and Social History of WWII Britain," author Janie Hampton described the Girl Guides' workday at MI5. Hampton wrote (Page 26-27):
Before a Guide could start work at MI5, she had to sign a contract confirming that she had permission from both of her parents and the Guide Captain who had recommended her. She pledged with her honour not to read the papers she carried, and was paid ten shillings a week for fifty hours of work, with only a short lunch break. The Guides' working day began at 9 a.m. and finished at 7 p.m., and as well as carrying messages they were responsible for keeping inkpots filled. Some were also trained to clean and repair typewriters.
The ten shilling note fell out of circulation in 1970 (Page 10) and was replaced by the 50 pence coin. A weekly pay of 50 pence in 1915, the first year the Girl Guides started working for MI5, was equivalent to £45.91, or roughly $62, in July 2026, according to the Bank of England.
The War Office also took Girl Guides to the signing of the Treaty of Versailles, which ended the state of war between Germany and the Allied Powers. Speaking about their work regarding the treaty, Hampton wrote (Page 29):
When the First World War ended, Guides were considered so reliable by the War Office that a contingent was taken with the British delegation to France. British Guides ran errands at the Palace of Versailles for the Paris Peace Conference in June 1919, and sixteen Ranger Guides were invited to witness the signing of the treaty.
For further reading, Snopes has previously investigated claims about Scouting America and the Girl Scouts of the USA.
